tcarac/taskboard:
# Taskboard

A local, self-hosted project management tool with a Kanban UI, full CLI, and a built-in [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) server that lets AI assistants manage your projects, tickets, and teams directly.

Single binary. SQLite-backed. No Docker, no external database, no runtime dependencies.

## Screenshots

![Kanban Board](screenshots/board.png)

![Ticket Detail](screenshots/ticket-detail.png)

## Features

- **Kanban Board** — drag-and-drop ticket management across Todo, In Progress, and Done columns
- **Projects** — organize work with customizable projects (icons, colors, prefixes)
- **Teams** — assign tickets to teams
- **Tickets** — priority levels, due dates, labels, subtasks, dependencies (blocked by)
- **Embedded Terminal** — run AI coding agents (opencode, Claude Code) directly from the web UI
- **CLI** — manage everything from the terminal
- **MCP Server** — 22 tools for AI-native project management via Model Context Protocol
- **Self-Hosted** — your data stays on your machine in a SQLite database
- **Single Binary** — one `brew install` and you're running

## Install

### Homebrew

```bash
brew tap tcarac/taskboard
brew install taskboard
```

### From source

```bash
git clone https://github.com/tcarac/taskboard.git
cd taskboard
make build
```

Requires Go 1.24+ and Node.js 22+.

## Usage

### Web UI

```bash
taskboard start
# => http://localhost:3010

taskboard start --port 8080
```

### CLI

```bash
taskboard project create "Auth System" --prefix AUTH --icon "🔐"
taskboard project list

taskboard ticket create --project <ID> --title "Implement login" --priority high
taskboard ticket list --project <ID> --status todo
taskboard ticket move <ID> --status done

taskboard team create "Backend"
taskboard team list
```

### MCP Server (for AI assistants)

```bash
taskboard mcp
```

#### Claude Code

```bash
claude mcp add taskboard -- /path/to/taskboard mcp
```

#### Claude Desktop

Add to `~/.claude/claude_desktop_config.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "taskboard": {
      "command": "/path/to/taskboard",
      "args": ["mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

#### Data Hierarchy

```
Project → Ticket → Subtask
(initiative)  (task)    (step)
```

- **Projects** are the top-level grouping (like epics/initiatives). Create one per body of work.
- **Tickets** are concrete, actionable tasks within a project. Don't create "epic" tickets — use projects.
- **Subtasks** are checklist steps within a ticket, for breaking work into verifiable pieces.

#### Available MCP Tools (22)

| Tool                    | Description                                      |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| **Projects**            |                                                  |
| `list_projects`         | List all projects with optional status filter    |
| `get_project`           | Get project details by ID                        |
| `create_project`        | Create a new project (use for epics/initiatives) |
| `update_project`        | Update project properties                        |
| `delete_project`        | Delete a project and all its tickets             |
| **Teams**               |                                                  |
| `list_teams`            | List all teams                                   |
| `get_team`              | Get team details by ID                           |
| `create_team`           | Create a new team                                |
| `update_team`           | Update team properties                           |
| `delete_team`           | Delete a team                                    |
| **Tickets**             |                                                  |
| `list_tickets`          | List tickets with filters                        |
| `get_ticket`            | Get ticket details with subtasks and labels      |
| `create_ticket`         | Create a ticket (task) within a project          |
| `update_ticket`         | Update ticket properties                         |
| `move_ticket`           | Move ticket to different status column           |
| `delete_ticket`         | Delete a ticket                                  |
| **Board**               |                                                  |
| `get_board`             | Get full Kanban board grouped by status          |
| **Subtasks**            |                                                  |
| `create_subtask`        | Add a subtask to a ticket                        |
| `batch_create_subtasks` | Add multiple subtasks to a ticket at once        |
| `toggle_subtask`        | Toggle subtask completion                        |
| `delete_subtask`        | Remove a subtask from a ticket                   |

#### Example Prompts

Once the MCP is connected, you can talk to your AI assistant in high-level terms and let it figure out the breakdown:

```
I'm building a SaaS billing system. Set up the project and break the work
into tickets covering Stripe integration, usage metering, invoice generation,
and a customer billing portal. Prioritize accordingly.
```

```
I need to ship a password reset flow. Think through what's involved — API
endpoints, email templates, token handling, UI screens, tests — and create
tickets with subtasks for each piece.
```

```
Look at my board and figure out what's blocking progress. If anything in
"in progress" has been sitting there without subtasks, break it down into
concrete next steps.
```

Here's what that looks like — a project and tickets created entirely by an AI assistant via MCP:

![Project created by AI](screenshots/project.png)

![Tickets list](screenshots/tickets.png)

### Embedded Terminal

The web UI includes a built-in terminal. Click **Terminal** in the sidebar to open a full PTY shell with color support and a resizable panel. Run `opencode`, `claude`, or any command directly from the browser.

![Embedded Terminal](screenshots/terminal.png)

The agent shares the same SQLite database via MCP, so tickets it creates show up on your board immediately.

## Data Storage

All data is stored in a SQLite database at:

- **macOS**: `~/Library/Application Support/taskboard/taskboard.db`
- **Linux**: `~/.config/taskboard/taskboard.db`

Migrations run automatically on first start.

### Custom Database Path

Use `--db` to point any command at a different database file:

```bash
taskboard --db /path/to/other.db start
taskboard --db /path/to/other.db mcp
taskboard --db /path/to/other.db ticket list
```

### Clearing Data

To wipe all projects, tickets, teams, and labels while keeping the schema intact:

```bash
taskboard clear        # prompts for confirmation
taskboard clear -f     # skip confirmation
```

This also respects `--db`, so you can clear a specific database file:

```bash
taskboard --db /tmp/test.db clear -f
```

## Tech Stack

| Layer        | Technology                                          |
| ------------ | --------------------------------------------------- |
| Language     | Go                                                  |
| Database     | SQLite (via modernc.org/sqlite, pure Go)            |
| CLI          | cobra                                               |
| HTTP         | chi                                                 |
| Frontend     | React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS v4, dnd-kit         |
| Terminal     | xterm.js, gorilla/websocket, creack/pty             |
| MCP          | JSON-RPC over stdio                                 |
| Distribution | Single binary with embedded frontend via `embed.FS` |

yaront1111/Moe-s-Tavern:
# Moe's Tavern

**An AI agent task board. Turn your coding agents into a team you can steer.**

Run Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, and Grok Build through a shared task board in your IDE. Give agents clear roles, review their plans, and follow the work through implementation and QA.

[![CI](https://github.com/yaront1111/Moe-s-Tavern/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/yaront1111/Moe-s-Tavern/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![MIT License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
![Platforms](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows%20%7C%20macOS%20%7C%20Linux-lightgrey.svg)
![Works with](https://img.shields.io/badge/works%20with-Claude%20Code%20%C2%B7%20Codex%20%C2%B7%20Gemini%20CLI%20%C2%B7%20Grok%20Build-6f42c1.svg)

**[Get started](#get-started) · [See the workflow](#how-it-works) · [Features](#what-you-get) · [Claude accounts](#run-claude-agents-across-several-accounts) · [Documentation](#documentation)**

> **New on `main`: Claude account rotation.** Sign in each of your Claude subscription accounts once, and Moe moves Claude Code agents to the next account when the active one reaches 90% of a usage window. Workers switch between steps, never mid-step, and the **Accounts** tab shows every account's 5-hour and weekly usage. [See how it works](#run-claude-agents-across-several-accounts).

![Moe's JetBrains board showing tasks grouped by epic across Backlog, Planning, Working, Review, and Done.](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cc68f17b-137f-42f3-b90c-eba0b68ba032)

*One place to see what is planned, what is being built, and what needs review.*

## Why Moe?

Working with several coding agents means keeping track of their tasks, context, plans, and results. Moe gives that work a shared workflow: you define the outcome, an architect proposes the approach, a worker implements it, and QA checks it against your Definition of Done.

Start with one small task. As you add agents, the same board keeps their plans, progress, conversations, and review feedback together. Choose the coding CLI for each role and decide how much approval you want to retain.

## What you get

| Feature | What it lets you do |
| --- | --- |
| **A live board inside your IDE** | Organize work into epics and tasks, inspect plans and implementation steps, and follow progress from Backlog to Done. JetBrains is the primary interface; a VS Code / Antigravity extension is also included. |
| **Plan approval before implementation** | Review proposed steps and affected files in the default **CONTROL** mode. Choose SPEED or TURBO when you want more automation. |
| **Agents with distinct jobs** | Give planning, implementation, and QA their own roles. Add a governor to help monitor the team and surface blockers. |
| **Your choice of coding CLI** | Launch Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, or Grok Build. Pick different providers for different roles. |
| **Several Claude accounts, one team** | Sign in each of your Claude subscription accounts once. Moe shows every account's 5-hour and weekly usage and moves Claude Code agents to the next account at a switch point you set, between steps and never mid-step. |
| **Coordination for parallel work** | Use teams, task dependencies, chat channels, and @mentions to coordinate agents. File overlap warnings help flag potential collisions. |
| **Context that survives a session** | Keep tasks, plans, decisions, and handoffs with your project. Add [Serena](docs/MEMORY.md) for shared agent memory across sessions. |
| **Git history tied to tasks** | Agent launchers create task-linked commits, checkpoints, and recovery refs so you can inspect what landed and investigate interrupted work. |
| **Project rules and reusable practices** | Configure project rules (rails) and role guidance. Bundled skills cover planning, testing, debugging, and review; global required and forbidden patterns are checked in submitted plans. |

Moe's daemon and project state run locally, with workflow data stored in `.moe/`. Your coding agents use their own providers and sign-ins, and Moe never handles their credentials; with [account rotation](#run-claude-agents-across-several-accounts), it only chooses which of your signed-in Claude accounts a new session starts on. Moe is MIT licensed; provider access and usage are separate.

## How it works

In the default **CONTROL** mode:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Task[You define a task] --> Plan[Architect proposes a plan]
    Plan --> Approve[You review and approve]
    Approve --> Build[Worker implements]
    Build --> Review[QA checks the result]
    Review --> Done[Done]
    Review -->|Changes requested| Build
```

| Role | Job |
| --- | --- |
| **Architect** | Explore the project and propose an implementation plan. |
| **Worker** | Implement the approved plan and record verification results. |
| **QA** | Review the result against the Definition of Done; approve it or request changes. |
| **Governor** | Monitor team activity, help resolve coordination problems, and escalate blockers. |

For a first task, ask Moe to document your project's setup and test commands. Review the architect's proposed scope, let the worker write the guide, then inspect QA's findings and the Git diff. Use the same workflow for features, bug fixes, and refactors.

## Get started

The first-run path below uses **JetBrains and one small task**. The [full walkthrough](docs/GETTING_STARTED.md) includes platform details and troubleshooting.

### Install a release

Download the plugin from the [latest GitHub Release](https://github.com/yaront1111/Moe-s-Tavern/releases/latest):

- **JetBrains** — `moe-jetbrains-<version>.zip`. Open **Settings / Preferences → Plugins → gear icon → Install Plugin from Disk**, select the ZIP, and restart the IDE.
- **VS Code / Antigravity** — `moe-vscode-<version>.vsix`. Install it with **Extensions: Install from VSIX**, open your target project, then run **Moe: Connect to Daemon**.

The plugins bundle their own daemon and proxy. You still need Node.js on PATH and one coding CLI (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, or Grok Build) installed and signed in. After installing, continue at [step 2](#2-open-the-board).

> JetBrains Marketplace, VS Code Marketplace, Open VSX, and npm listings are not published yet. [Claude account rotation](#run-claude-agents-across-several-accounts) arrived after v0.8.0; [build from source](#1-build-from-source) to use it before the next release.

### 1. Build from source

Download the [source ZIP](https://github.com/yaront1111/Moe-s-Tavern/archive/refs/heads/main.zip), extract it, and open a terminal in the extracted Moe folder. You can also clone this repository.

**Windows — PowerShell:**

```powershell
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\scripts\install-all.ps1 -BuildPlugin
```

**macOS / Linux:**

```bash
bash scripts/install-mac.sh --global --skip-mcp --with-plugin
```

The installer sets up Git, Node.js/npm, package dependencies, the daemon and proxy, the selected agent CLI, and JDK 17 for the plugin build. It also builds the JetBrains plugin ZIP. On Linux, it installs tmux for agent terminals. Existing compatible dependencies are reused.

You need a JetBrains IDE and your platform's package manager: **WinGet on Windows**, **Homebrew and Xcode Command Line Tools on macOS**, or **apt/dnf on Linux**. The script may request administrator access when installing system packages. If a prerequisite cannot be installed, it stops with instructions.

**Claude Code is the default.** To choose another bootstrap option, append the corresponding flag:

| Agent | Windows | macOS / Linux |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Codex | `-AgentCommand codex` | `--agent codex` |
| Gemini CLI | `-AgentCommand gemini` | `--agent gemini` |
| Skip agent installation | `-AgentCommand none` | `--agent none` |

Grok Build is supported by the agent launchers. The Windows installer also accepts `-AgentCommand grok`; on macOS/Linux, install Grok Build separately.

Keep the Moe folder after installation. Open a **new terminal**, go to your target project, and run your selected coding CLI once to sign in to your provider account.

**Terminal only?** Leave off `-BuildPlugin` or `--with-plugin`. The installer still puts `moe-daemon` and `moe-proxy` on your PATH; run `moe-daemon init --project .` inside your project to create `.moe/` and keep the daemon running in that terminal.

### 2. Open the board

1. If you built from source: in JetBrains, open **Settings / Preferences → Plugins → gear icon → Install Plugin from Disk**.
2. Select the ZIP in `moe-jetbrains/build/distributions/` and restart the IDE. (If you installed a release ZIP, skip 1–2.)
3. Open **your target Git project**, then open the **Moe** tool window. The plugin initializes `.moe/` and starts the daemon. Wait for **Connected**.

The ZIP and `.vsix` attached to each [GitHub Release](https://github.com/yaront1111/Moe-s-Tavern/releases) are built from that release's tag. If you built from source, install the plugin you built so it matches your checkout.

### 3. Run your first task

1. Open **Project Settings** and keep **Approval Mode: CONTROL**.
2. Click **+ Epic**, create an epic such as `First task`, then use the **+** in its **Backlog** column to create a task. Give it a clear description and Definition of Done.
3. Drag the task to **Planning**. In **Agents**, choose **Architect**, then your installed CLI. Architects claim tasks in Planning, so a task left in Backlog will wait.
4. When the task shows **Awaiting Approval**, open it, read the plan, and click **Approve**.
5. Launch **Worker** and **QA** from the same menu. Keep their terminals open and follow the task through **Working → Review → Done**.

Open the completed task to inspect its steps, verification results, and QA summary, then review the changed files and recorded commit in Git. By default, the launchers commit task changes and attempt to push them; check any reported Git or verification failure before treating the task as delivered.

Once one task completes, use **Agents → All Agents** to start the team together. Have more than one Claude subscription account? [Add them in the **Accounts** tab](#run-claude-agents-across-several-accounts) first, so the team can move between them. If a step stalls, use the [first-task troubleshooting guide](docs/GETTING_STARTED.md#when-a-step-does-not-work).

<details>
<summary>Launch agents from external terminals</summary>

Open a new terminal in the Moe checkout and run one role per terminal. Change `architect` to `worker` or `qa` for the next roles.

**Windows:**

```powershell
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\scripts\moe-agent.ps1 -Role architect -Project "C:\your\project"
```

**macOS / Linux:**

```bash
./scripts/moe-agent.sh --role architect --project "/your/project"
```

These examples use Claude Code. For Codex, add `-Command codex` on Windows or `--command codex` on macOS/Linux. The launchers configure the agent's Moe connection and start the daemon if needed.

A codex seat runs the interactive terminal UI for every role, and it commits nothing while that UI is open — the launcher records the commit after the CLI exits, so the task can reach **Done** on the board while Git still shows no commit for it. Close the terminal UI and the commit appears; to run a codex seat unattended so it lands a commit per task, add `-CodexExec` on Windows or `--codex-exec` on macOS/Linux (that headless launch has its own sandbox and approval settings — see [`MOE_CODEX_SANDBOX`](docs/CONFIGURATION.md#agent-scripts)).

</details>

<details>
<summary>Use VS Code / Antigravity</summary>

Install the `.vsix` from the [latest GitHub Release](https://github.com/yaront1111/Moe-s-Tavern/releases/latest), or build the [VS Code / Antigravity extension](moe-vscode/README.md) from source: run the installer above, then open a new terminal in the Moe folder:

**Windows:**

```powershell
cd moe-vscode
npm.cmd install
npm.cmd run package
```

**macOS / Linux:**

```bash
cd moe-vscode
npm install
npm run package
```

Use **Extensions: Install from VSIX** to install the resulting `.vsix`, open your target project, then run **Moe: Connect to Daemon**. See the extension's README for board commands and connection options. The **Accounts** tab is JetBrains-only; in VS Code, manage Claude accounts with `moe-daemon accounts` from a terminal. JetBrains is the primary first-run path documented here.

</details>

## Choose your level of control

Set the approval mode in **Project Settings**:

| Mode | Plan approval | Best when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **CONTROL** — default | You review and approve plans before implementation. | You are getting started or want to inspect each approach. |
| **SPEED** | Plans are automatically approved after a configurable delay, giving you a window to intervene. | You want plans to move forward automatically with a review window. |
| **TURBO** | Submitted plans are automatically approved immediately. | You want autonomous plan approval for a scope you have already defined. |

Agent review and project rules support your workflow. Inspect the results and keep your normal repository checks and merge protections.

## Run Claude agents across several accounts

> **New on `main`**, not in v0.8.0. [Build from source](#1-build-from-source) to use it before the next release.

Have more than one Claude subscription account? Sign each one in once, and Moe picks the account each Claude Code session starts on. It fills the accounts in your order and moves to the next one once any usage window of the active account (5-hour or weekly) reaches the switch point, 90% by default.

**In JetBrains:** in the Moe tool window, open **Accounts** and click **Add...**. Name the account, and a terminal tab opens with Claude's own sign-in (`claude auth login --claudeai`); finish it in your browser. Repeat for each account, put them in order with **Move up** and **Move down**, and change **Switch to the next account at** if 90% doesn't suit you. Then launch agents as usual.

**From a terminal**, after a [source install](#1-build-from-source):

```bash
moe-daemon accounts add --label "Personal"   # prints the new id, e.g. acct-1
moe-daemon accounts login acct-1             # Claude's own sign-in for that account
moe-daemon accounts check                    # exits 0 when every account is on a subscription
```

- **No step is cut short.** A worker whose account reaches the switch point finishes its current step and ends its session. The launcher restarts the same task on the next account, and the new session picks up at the next step. QA, architect, and governor seats move at their next launch.
- **Limits are handled for you.** If Claude refuses a launch at its limit, the launcher retries on the next account at once. When every account is spent, agents keep their tasks and resume at the earliest reset.
- **You always know which account is in use.** The **Accounts** tab shows each account's sign-in, 5-hour and weekly usage, and status. The tool-window header shows the active account, worker cards name theirs, and `#governors` gets a 🔁 post on every switch.
- **Credentials stay with Claude.** Each account is its own Claude config folder under `~/.moe/claude-accounts/`. Moe creates the folder and hands its path to Claude; it never reads, copies, or stores a login.
- **Off until you sign an account in.** Until then, or whenever Bedrock, Vertex, or Foundry is configured, Claude launches exactly as before. `MOE_ACCOUNT_ROTATION=off` turns rotation off. Codex, Gemini CLI, and Grok Build seats are unaffected.

One account list serves every project on the machine. Each account folder takes the place of `~/.claude` for its sessions, so add any user-level settings, `CLAUDE.md`, agents, skills, or plugins your agents rely on to each folder.

> **Use your own accounts, within Anthropic's terms.** Rotation only chooses which of your accounts a new session starts on; it never raises a limit. Pro and Max limits [assume ordinary, individual use](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/legal-and-compliance), and logins [may not be shared](https://www.anthropic.com/legal/consumer-terms), so check that your setup fits before relying on it. If you run a large, always-on fleet, API keys or a Team or Enterprise plan are the better fit.

More: [rotation rules](docs/MCP_SERVER.md#claude-account-rotation) · [environment variables](docs/CONFIGURATION.md#environment-variables) · [troubleshooting](docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md#claude-account-rotation-issues).

## Extend Moe

Moe connects its IDE interfaces and coding agents through a local TypeScript daemon and an MCP proxy. Use the [MCP reference](docs/MCP_SERVER.md) and [architecture guide](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) to build integrations or understand the runtime.

Customize [role guidance](docs/roles/) and [agent skills](docs/skills/) for your project. Optionally connect [Serena](docs/MEMORY.md) for code navigation and shared memory.

A local-first command center for software projects.

Download Shipyard · Run from source · Contribute

## Why Shipyard? Development work is spread across editors, terminal windows, Git clients, task boards, and AI tools. Shipyard brings the operational layer together without trying to replace your editor. - **Local-first** — the dashboard and API run on your machine; project and task data stays in local JSON files. - **Portfolio view** — see every project, active task, branch, and working tree from one place. - **Fast project switching** — keep many workspaces open; project tabs share the available width and stay visible. - **Built for coding agents** — hand a task to Claude Code, Codex, Aider, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Cursor CLI, or your own CLI, each in its own Git worktree if you want, then review what it changed. - **No database required** — installation, backup, inspection, and recovery remain straightforward. - **Cross-platform** — desktop installers for Windows, macOS, and Linux with automatic updates, plus browser-based development mode. ## Highlights | Area | What Shipyard provides | |---|---| | Dashboard | Project health, Git state, detected stack, task counts, favorites, deploy status, and a 24-hour feed of what agents started, noted, and finished | | Tasks | Milestone-scoped Kanban boards, priorities, effort points, time forecasts, subtasks, technical prompts, search, and a global task view | | Agents | Run a task with any registered coding CLI, add a one-off instruction, optionally isolate it in a per-task Git worktree, and review its commits afterwards | | Git | Status, diffs, history, branches, stage/unstage, commit, pull, push, and projects with many nested repositories | | Terminals | Integrated xterm sessions, split panes, native launchers, dev servers, AI-written tab names, and an alert when an agent asks a question or finishes | | Files | Lazy file tree, previews, editing, filename search, and content search | | AI | Claude, OpenAI, and Gemini with automatic fallback; subscription CLIs first, API keys as a paid fallback | | MCP | OAuth-protected server with 29 tools for projects, milestones, tasks, Git, Trello attachments, and sync | | Sync | Milestone-scoped Google Sheets, Trello, and ClickUp integrations | | Deploys | Read-only Railway status per service, linked automatically by GitHub repository | | Cloud sync | Optional end-to-end encrypted sync of projects, tasks, and settings between your machines | | Desktop | Electron app with tray, native shortcuts, automatic updates, and platform installers | ### A terminal designed for AI workflows The integrated terminal includes WebGL rendering, output batching, safe bracketed paste, reconnect handling, split panes, and session persistence. Clipboard images can be pasted with `Ctrl+V`: Shipyard stores the image temporarily on your machine and inserts its path into the agent's prompt. Shipyard reads each terminal's screen. When Claude Code waits for an answer, the tab shows an amber question mark; when it finishes a job, a green check. Tabs opened for a task carry its number and title, and other tabs get a short name written by AI from their output (optional). ### Minimal, scalable interface Primary actions stay visible; secondary actions live in contextual menus. Project tabs share the available width instead of scrolling sideways, so every open project stays one click away. ## Download Use the latest CI-built installers from the [Releases page](https://github.com/defremont/Shipyard/releases/latest). | Platform | Installer | |---|---| | Windows x64 | `Shipyard-Setup-.exe` | | macOS Apple Silicon | `Shipyard--arm64.dmg` | | macOS Intel | `Shipyard--x64.dmg` | | Linux x64 | `Shipyard-.AppImage` or `Shipyard-.deb` | Installed apps check for new releases at startup and every four hours, download them in the background, and offer a restart (macOS updates require a signed build; on Linux only the AppImage updates itself). Release builds support Windows Authenticode signing and macOS Developer ID signing/notarization. Maintainers must configure the repository secrets described in [Release signing](#release-signing); unsigned local builds may still show the operating system's security warning. ## Run from source ### Requirements - [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) 20 LTS or newer - [pnpm](https://pnpm.io/installation) - [Git](https://git-scm.com/) ```bash git clone https://github.com/defremont/Shipyard.git cd Shipyard pnpm install pnpm dev ``` Open [http://localhost:5421](http://localhost:5421). The frontend runs on port `5421` and the Fastify API on `5420`. Setup helpers are also available: ```bash # Linux / macOS chmod +x setup.sh devdash.sh ./setup.sh ./devdash.sh # Windows setup.cmd devdash.cmd ``` The first-run wizard helps discover project folders and explains the main workspace controls. ### Optional integrated terminal The browser terminal uses `node-pty`, which is installed as an optional native dependency. If it is unavailable, the rest of Shipyard continues to work and terminal actions fall back to native operating-system terminals. ## Core workflows ### Manage projects Add existing folders or scan a parent directory. Shipyard detects Git repositories, common technologies, branches, local changes, remotes, and one-level nested repositories. Favorite important projects or jump to any workspace with `Ctrl+K`. ### Plan and execute tasks Each project has a virtual **General** milestone and can define additional milestones. Tasks move through Inbox, In Progress, and Done while preserving cascading timestamps. The description captures the product outcome; the technical prompt captures implementation context for a developer or coding agent. Tasks can carry an effort size (1, 2, 3, 5, or 8). Shipyard uses your own history of finished tasks to forecast how long the open ones will take, and shows the totals on each Kanban column. ### Work with Git Inspect changes, review diffs, stage files, commit, synchronize with remotes, and browse history without leaving the workspace. Projects that hold several independent repositories get a filterable repository picker, and Shipyard remembers the last one you chose. ### Hand tasks to coding agents **Run with AI** opens the task in a terminal with a generated prompt: project context, the task, and the MCP tools the agent should use to report progress. Before it starts you can pick the agent and add a decision that overrides the task description for that run. - **Agents** — Claude Code, Codex CLI, Aider, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, and Cursor CLI are built in. Add your own command under **Settings**; argument templates accept `{cwd}`, `{task}`, and `{taskFile}`. - **Worktree per task** — optional. Each task gets its own branch and Git worktree, so several agents can work on one repository at once. Worktrees of tasks done for more than seven days are removed automatically, unless they hold uncommitted changes. - **Review** — the task's Review tab lists the commits and files changed between the moment it started and the moment it finished. Expand a commit to see its diff; **Needs changes** adds a dated note and sends the task back to In Progress. ### Use AI features Shipyard supports Claude, OpenAI, and Gemini. You choose a preferred provider; if it fails, the next one takes over. Within each provider Shipyard uses your subscription CLI first (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI) and a configured API key only as a paid fallback. You can: - chat with project context; - analyze tasks and generate implementation prompts; - organize or update several tasks from plain text; - size tasks by effort in bulk and review the suggestions before saving; - generate commit messages from the current diff. With a Claude subscription, a small ring in the sidebar shows how much of the five-hour usage window you have used. AI features are optional; project, task, Git, file, and terminal management work without them. ### Connect through MCP Shipyard includes a Model Context Protocol server with OAuth 2.1 and PKCE. Compatible agents can list projects and milestones, create, update, and bulk-edit tasks, log progress notes, inspect Git state, reorder work, read Trello comments and image attachments, and trigger configured sync providers. Connection instructions and consent controls are available under **Settings → MCP**. ### Synchronize milestones Integrations are isolated by `(project, provider, milestone)`, so each milestone can connect to a different remote board, list, or sheet. | Provider | Direction | Notes | |---|---|---| | Google Sheets | Bidirectional | Apps Script bridge, timestamp merge, automatic push and pull | | Trello | Bidirectional | Board/list mapping, controlled card ordering, remote edit protection, retry handling | | ClickUp | Bidirectional | List mapping with project and milestone isolation | Trello comments and attachments are pulled into the task (read-only), so an agent can see the screenshot a client attached to the card. Credentials are configured once per provider; mappings and synchronization state remain local. Shipyard only reads from Railway; it never redeploys or rolls back. ### Sync between machines **Shipyard Cloud** is an optional hosted service that keeps projects, tasks, milestones, and settings in step across your computers. It is off until you sign in under **Settings → Cloud sync**. Your password never leaves the machine: data is encrypted before upload, and the server stores only encrypted blobs. There is no password reset — if you lose it, you lose the cloud copy, while each machine keeps its data. To move a whole setup instead, `pnpm workspace:export` packs Shipyard's data, the Git remotes to clone, bundles of repositories with no remote, and ignored `.env` files; `workspace-import.mjs`, shipped inside the bundle, restores it on the other machine. ## Keyboard shortcuts | Shortcut | Action | |---|---| | `Ctrl+K` | Search projects, tasks, and files | | `Ctrl+Shift+F` | Search file contents | | `Ctrl+Backtick` | Toggle the integrated terminal | | `?` | Show every shortcut | | `Ctrl+N` | New task in the active project (desktop app) | | `Ctrl+W` | Close the active editor or project tab (desktop app) | | `Ctrl+Enter` | Save the task dialog from any field | | `Ctrl+S` | Save the open file | | `Ctrl+V` | Paste text or a clipboard image into the terminal | | `Shift` + drag | Select terminal text while mouse tracking is active | Browsers reserve `Ctrl+N` and `Ctrl+W`, so those two work only in the desktop app. On macOS, use `Cmd` for application shortcuts where applicable. ## Data and privacy Shipyard does not require an account or a hosted database. Shipyard Cloud is opt-in and end-to-end encrypted. In development mode, data is written under `data/`. Desktop builds store it in the operating system's application-data directory. The main files are plain JSON and can be backed up with normal filesystem tools. ```text data/ ├── projects.json ├── settings.json ├── tasks/ │ └── .json ├── ai-config.json # encrypted API keys ├── sync-config.json ├── deploy-config.json # encrypted Railway token ├── cloud-sync.json # encrypted Shipyard Cloud session ├── mcp-config.json ├── mcp-auth.json └── server.log ``` Third-party features communicate only with the provider you configure, such as Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Trello, ClickUp, or Railway. Review those providers' privacy policies before enabling an integration. ## Architecture ```text ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ React + Vite client │ │ dashboard · tasks · Git · files · terminal · agents · AI │ └──────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘ │ REST / SSE / WebSocket ┌──────────────────────────────▼──────────────────────────────┐ │ Fastify server │ │ routes · services · MCP · PTY · sync · AI · deploy · cloud │ └───────────────┬──────────────────────────────┬──────────────┘ │ │ ┌────────▼────────┐ ┌────────▼────────┐ │ Local JSON data │ │ Local projects │ │ atomic + locked │ │ Git + filesystem│ └─────────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ ``` | Layer | Technology | |---|---| | Frontend | React 18, Vite, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui, React Query | | Backend | Fastify 5, TypeScript, Zod, simple-git | | Terminal | xterm.js, WebSocket, optional node-pty | | Desktop | Electron, electron-builder, electron-updater | | Persistence | Atomic JSON stores with in-process mutation locks | | Monorepo | pnpm workspaces | ### Repository layout ```text client/src/ React application, components, hooks, and API client server/src/ Fastify routes and domain services electron/ Desktop process, preload bridge, and packaging hooks scripts/ Workspace export/import between machines assets/ Icons and README media data/ Local development data (generated and gitignored) .github/workflows Release automation for Windows, macOS, and Linux ``` ## Development ```bash pnpm dev # frontend + backend with watch mode pnpm build # production client, server, and Electron build pnpm dist:win # Windows installer pnpm dist:mac # macOS DMGs pnpm dist:linux # Linux AppImage and deb ``` The codebase intentionally avoids a database and keeps its data stores recoverable. Before contributing architecture, route, model, or convention changes, read [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md). ## Contributing Contributions, bug reports, and focused feature proposals are welcome. 1. Fork the repository. 2. Create a branch from `main`. 3. Install dependencies with `pnpm install`. 4. Make a scoped change and update documentation when behavior changes. 5. Run `pnpm build` and test the affected workflow. 6. Open a pull request explaining the problem, solution, and validation. UI changes should use the existing design tokens and shadcn/ui primitives. New task mutations must invalidate both project tasks and the global task query. New JSON stores must use serialized mutations and atomic writes. ## Release process Pushing a `v*` tag starts the GitHub Actions release workflow. It builds Windows, macOS Intel/Apple Silicon, AppImage, and Debian artifacts, then creates a draft GitHub release with generated notes, installers, and the `latest*.yml` update manifests. Installed apps ignore drafts: publishing the draft is what releases the update. ### Release signing For Windows, add `WIN_CSC_LINK` (a path/URL or base64-encoded PFX) and `WIN_CSC_KEY_PASSWORD` as GitHub Actions secrets. An OV certificate identifies the publisher but can still need time to build SmartScreen reputation; an EV certificate provides immediate reputation. Keep the certificate subject stable between releases. For macOS, add `MAC_CSC_LINK`, `MAC_CSC_KEY_PASSWORD`, `APPLE_API_KEY` (the base64-encoded contents of the `.p8` key), `APPLE_API_KEY_ID`, `APPLE_API_ISSUER`, and `APPLE_TEAM_ID`. The certificate must be a **Developer ID Application** certificate for direct DMG distribution. The build uses Hardened Runtime, submits it to Apple for notarization, and staples the resulting ticket. The application ID (`com.shipyard.dev`), product name, executable name, and Linux desktop filename are intentionally stable. Changing one of them is a migration and can break Windows taskbar pins, macOS preferences, Linux launcher association, or the upgrade path. ## License Shipyard is available under the [Apache License 2.0](LICENSE). If Shipyard improves your development workflow, consider [starring the repository](https://github.com/defremont/Shipyard) or sharing what you build with it.

# Task Rail

**A compact Windows task board for you and your coding agents.** Track each project in three columns, adjust progress on a card, and let Codex or Claude Code update the same board through MCP. Keep the widget on top or tuck it behind a screen edge; share a project when teammates need the same tasks.

[![Build](https://github.com/kirgx/task-rail/actions/workflows/build.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/kirgx/task-rail/actions/workflows/build.yml) [![Release antivirus scan](https://github.com/kirgx/task-rail/actions/workflows/release-antivirus.yml/badge.svg?event=release)](https://github.com/kirgx/task-rail/actions/workflows/release-antivirus.yml?query=event%3Arelease) [![ZIP downloads](assets/downloads.svg)](https://github.com/kirgx/task-rail/releases) [![MIT license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-1b1c1f?labelColor=1b1c1f&color=19d76b)](LICENSE)

ZIP downloads counts GitHub release ZIP downloads, not installations. GitHub Actions refreshes the count daily and when a release is published.
The antivirus badge shows the latest release scan. The workflow verifies the ZIP's SHA-256 checksum, extracts it, and scans its files with ClamAV; click the badge for the result. One antivirus scan cannot guarantee that software is safe.

## Quick start

1. Download the latest Windows x64 ZIP from [Releases](https://github.com/kirgx/task-rail/releases), extract it, and run `install.ps1` in PowerShell. The package includes the app and MCP bridge; no .NET SDK is needed.
2. Create a project tab, add a task, and move it across **To do**, **In progress**, and **Done**.
3. To connect installed Codex and Claude Code CLIs, run `.\setup-agent.ps1 -UseInstalled` from the extracted folder and restart their sessions. See the [agent setup guide](docs/AGENT_SETUP.md) to link a repository and add project rules.

You can give an agent this repository URL and ask it to follow [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) and the setup guide. Local boards stay on your Windows account; sharing a project with a teammate is optional.

## The board

![Task Rail showing a project with tasks in To Do, In Progress, and Done](task-widget/preview-board-en.png)

*Task Rail v1.5.11 with illustrative tasks. No personal project data is shown.*

1. Create a project tab and type a task at the top. Pick an **Epic** if it belongs to a larger piece of work; new tasks start in **To do**.
2. Drag a card to **In progress** or **Done**. Drag its colored side bar to adjust progress, or open the card to add a description, acceptance criteria, and work notes. Each column scrolls on its own.
3. Use a task number such as `#42` when talking to an agent. Codex and Claude Code can read and update the same board through the local MCP server. Task versions catch conflicting edits; the card shows who last moved it.
4. Keep the widget on top, resize it, or drag it partly beyond a screen edge. It leaves a small tab you can pull back from any edge, including on a second monitor. It remembers where you put it and can start with Windows.

Double-click a card to edit its details:

![Task details with title, description, acceptance criteria, and work notes](task-widget/preview-details-en.png)

Deleted cards go to an archive and can be restored with their task number and progress. Task colors help distinguish work at a glance.

Use **Epic** beside the task field to assign an existing epic or create one. Open a card to change its epic later. The color dot in an epic header offers five colors. Its header shows the average progress of its cards; an epic folds within each column. Existing tasks with the same leading tag, such as `THT:`, still fold together. Click a task number to copy it.
The most recently changed task or epic appears first. Agent activity checks do not change the order.

## Usage limits

Click the striped usage icon in the title bar to open the Claude and Codex panels. Each line shows the percentage of a reported limit still available and the time until its automatic reset. **RESETS** shows the number of manual reset credits the service reports; a dash means the count is unavailable. Task Rail shows only the time windows each client provides. These are usage-limit percentages, not exact token balances. The panel starts hidden and refreshes every five minutes while open.

![Sample Claude and Codex usage limits, reset times, and manual reset credits](task-widget/preview-usage-en.png)

*Illustrative values. This screenshot contains no account usage data.*

## Agent library

Click the library icon beside it to read global and project `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` files, other project Markdown files, and locally installed Codex and Claude skills and plugins. Use **Project folder** to link a repository to each project tab. The library reads files without editing them.

![Library with sample project rules and Rules, Skills, and Plugins tabs](task-widget/preview-library-en.png)

A project activity dot shows when a connected local agent is working, waiting for input, or idle. Double-click a project tab to rename it.

The interface is in English. Personal projects stay on this Windows account; shared projects synchronize through a server. The invite key grants edit access to one shared project.

## Share a project

Each person runs Task Rail on their own Windows PC and connects their own coding agents through the local MCP bridge. The shared server stores one project's tasks, and both widgets refresh every five seconds. Other projects remain on each person's PC.

For two people on the same private network or VPN:

1. On the PC with the project, select its tab and click **Share** above the columns, then **Host on this PC**. Task Rail copies its existing tasks to the shared board.
2. Click **Copy invite** and send the link to your teammate.
3. Your teammate creates an empty project tab, opens **Share**, enters their name, pastes the link, and clicks **Join project**. Each person links their own repository folder through **Library** → **Project folder**. Repeat this step for each additional teammate.

Keep Task Rail running on the host PC. Closing its window to the tray keeps hosting active; **Exit** stops the server. For an always-on board over the internet, use the included [Docker Compose setup](compose.yaml) with a domain, persistent storage, and HTTPS, or deploy the [Dockerfile](Dockerfile) on a host that provides HTTPS. One server hosts one shared project.

People can edit different cards at the same time. If two people save the same card, the second save is rejected and its draft stays on that PC for comparison. The invite link grants edit access to the whole project; it is a shared key, not an individual account. See [sharing setup](docs/SHARING.md) for deployment, updates, backups, and conflict recovery.

## Install on Windows x64

From a clone, install the .NET 10 SDK and run `.\setup-agent.ps1` in PowerShell. It builds and installs Task Rail, then registers MCP for installed Codex and Claude Code CLIs. See the [agent setup guide](docs/AGENT_SETUP.md) for the full workflow.

For the packaged release, download the latest `TaskRail-v*-win-x64.zip` from [Releases](https://github.com/kirgx/task-rail/releases), extract it, and run `install.ps1` from the extracted folder. Run `.\setup-agent.ps1 -UseInstalled` to connect installed agent CLIs. The package is self-contained and needs no .NET SDK. The installer copies the app to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\TaskRail`, enables launch at sign-in, and starts it.

You can also run `widget\TaskWidget.exe` directly from the extracted folder without installing it. In that case, launch at sign-in is not configured.

Task Rail checks the latest GitHub release at startup and every 12 hours while running. When a newer version exists, a green **Update · v…** button appears beside the installed version in the title bar. Click it to open the release page, download and extract the newer ZIP, then run its `install.ps1`. The installer asks the running widget to exit normally before replacing files and starts the updated app. Your boards remain in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\TaskRail`. If an MCP file is in use, restart the connected agent sessions after updating. Updates are not installed automatically.

These GitHub builds are currently unsigned, so Windows may show an unrecognized publisher warning. Review the source and release checksum before running downloaded software.

## Connect a coding agent

Install the widget first, then run either command in PowerShell:

```powershell
codex mcp add task-rail -- "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\TaskRail\mcp\v9\TaskRail.Mcp.exe"
claude mcp add --scope user task-rail -- "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\TaskRail\mcp\v9\TaskRail.Mcp.exe"
```

Restart the agent session after adding MCP. The widget must be running for MCP requests. Use `ensure_project` to create or link a tab to the repository's absolute folder, then follow the [agent workflow](docs/AGENT_SETUP.md#3-put-the-workflow-in-the-projects-rules). Before changing an existing card, read it and pass its current `version` as `expected_version`; on a conflict, read it again. See the [widget guide](task-widget/README.md) for activity hooks and board controls.

## Build from source

Requires Windows and the .NET 10 SDK:

```powershell
dotnet build task-widget/TaskWidget.csproj -c Release
dotnet build task-rail-mcp/TaskRail.Mcp.csproj -c Release
dotnet build task-rail-server/TaskRail.Server.csproj -c Release
```

To create a self-contained release ZIP and SHA-256 checksum, run `./release.ps1` from the repository root. Output is written to `dist/`. The package contains the widget, MCP bridge, shared-board server, installation scripts, guides, README, and license.

## Data and privacy

Personal boards and window settings stay under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\TaskRail`. Shared tasks also live on the host you choose; the local copy contains an invite key. No board is stored in this repository. The MCP bridge uses a local named pipe restricted to the current Windows user. Opening the optional usage panel reads local Claude credentials to request usage data from Anthropic and invokes the local Codex client for its usage data. The widget does not store those credentials. See [PRIVACY.md](PRIVACY.md) for details.

## Project

Task Rail is licensed under [MIT](LICENSE). See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) before opening a pull request. Microsoft Store packaging is not part of this release.

# Switch

**Keep track of delegated work without keeping a window open for every conversation.**

English · [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

Switch is a local task board for Codex and Claude Code sessions. Group work by priority, see what is running or waiting, and read the latest reply before deciding whether to return to the original conversation. It is useful with one client and many tasks; mixing clients is optional.

![Switch with example sessions in the dark theme](docs/images/switch-dark.png)

*Example data. No real conversations are shown.*

## What it does

- **One view of your work.** Priority, Later and Unsorted columns, drag ordering, and independent scrolling.
- **Read before switching.** Expand multiple cards to read their latest complete replies. New replies load automatically; unchanged replies keep their reading position.
- **Choose what interrupts you.** Only Priority sessions send optional desktop alerts and count toward the App badge.
- **Return to the conversation.** Open Desktop sessions directly, or copy a CLI resume command. Creating tasks, replying and approving actions stay in the original client.
- **Make it yours.** Chinese/English and light/dark switches, saved groups and ordering, and settings import/export.

Switch reads local session records. It makes no model calls and does not upload conversations. The Python backend uses only the standard library; the browser renderer is bundled in the repository.

## Get started

You need **Python 3.9+**, a browser, and local Codex or Claude Code sessions. There is no `pip install`, Node.js requirement, or desktop framework to install for normal use.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/Simon-Wong-hjz/switch.git
cd switch
python3 taskboard.py
```

You can also [download the source ZIP](https://github.com/Simon-Wong-hjz/switch/archive/refs/heads/main.zip), extract it and run the last command there. On Windows, use `python` if that is your Python command.

The command opens `http://127.0.0.1:8765/`. Choose the sessions to add, then drag them into a group. New sessions created after the board is initialized are added automatically unless previously removed. The service refreshes data every five seconds; the refresh button requests an immediate scan.

Keep the terminal running, or enable the optional macOS login service below. Press Ctrl-C to stop, or run `python3 taskboard.py stop` from another terminal. For another port, use `python3 taskboard.py run --port 8766`; add `--no-open` to avoid opening a browser.

**Platform status:** used and tested on macOS with Python 3.12 and Edge. Chrome supports the browser App entry, but its complete installation and removal flow has not been manually verified here. Windows paths are implemented; real Windows client, installation and uninstall checks are still pending. Treat Windows as experimental. The interface is bilingual; command-line messages are currently Chinese.

## Install as an App

Click **Install app** in the board's top bar. It explains the benefits, then opens the browser's install dialog when available, or shows Edge/Chrome instructions.

Installing gives Switch its own Dock or taskbar entry and a separate window. The icon can show the number of Priority sessions needing attention where badges are supported. The App and browser page share the same board settings.

The App **does not start the Python backend** and is not always on top. Keep its window and the backend running for alerts and badge updates. Minimized is fine, but a suspended page cannot keep data current. Use the same host and port: `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, and different ports are separate browser App addresses.

## Optional setup

### Start at login on macOS

```sh
python3 taskboard.py autostart on
```

This starts Switch in the background now and at future logins. It keeps an existing configured port, or uses 8765. macOS restarts it after an abnormal exit. `stop` shuts it down normally until the next login; `autostart on` resumes it. Use `autostart off` to stop it and disable login startup. Windows login startup is not implemented yet.

### Add client hooks

The board works by reading local records without hooks. Hooks provide additional lifecycle events:

```sh
python3 taskboard.py setup
python3 taskboard.py status
```

Setup lists proposed changes and asks before applying them. Use `--only codex` or `--only claude` to choose a client. Codex may require trusting the hooks through `/hooks`. Hooks record events; they do not answer questions or approve actions. `setup --yes` skips the interactive confirmation for an installation you have already authorized. It does not enable login startup; that requires `--autostart` explicitly.

You can give an Agent this installation request:

> Install Switch from https://github.com/Simon-Wong-hjz/switch in a directory I choose. Follow its README, check Python, start it, and report the URL and uninstall command. Ask before enabling client hooks or login startup. Do not change my clients' notification settings.

## Alerts and read state

Enable alerts from the Priority column header. **Only Priority sessions notify and count toward the App badge.** Later and Unsorted cards still display their states. Switch does not change the clients' own notifications. Use **Test alert** to check browser and operating-system permissions; **Mute while board has focus** is optional and off by default.

Alerts cover new final replies, new questions and confirmed Claude Code approval waits. Existing states do not notify on page load or when moving a card into Priority. Alerts require an open board page and a running backend.

Codex Desktop conversations follow Codex's current read state on every refresh: listed as unread keeps the new-reply flag, otherwise the reply shows as read, including a reply that finished in a conversation you already had open. Marking a reply unread in Codex restores its flag; reading it again clears it. If Codex's state file is missing, unreadable, in an unknown format, signed out, or older than the reply, Switch keeps what it last knew and does not assume the reply was read. CLI sessions have no reliable read signal. Use **Mark this reply as read**, **Open**, or **Copy resume command** to acknowledge the reply in Switch. Expanding a card alone does not mark it read. Reading an older reply does not clear a newer one.

## Local files and clean removal

| Location | What Switch writes |
| --- | --- |
| `data/` inside this directory | Settings, cached board data, bounded hook logs, service records and startup logs |
| Codex `hooks.json` / Claude `settings.json` | Only optional hook entries owned by this installation |
| `~/Library/LaunchAgents/local.switch.<installation-id>.plist` | Only when macOS login startup is enabled |
| Browser-managed storage | Browser App registration, history, permissions and temporary page state |

Client conversations are read-only. Switch does not modify PATH or shell profiles. `status` lists the external integrations. Settings live in `data/settings.json`; export/import them from **Settings file** to move a board between installations.

To remove Switch:

1. If installed as an App, uninstall it from the App menu or browser's app manager.
2. Run the command below. It stops the backend, disables its login service, removes its unchanged hook entries and deletes its data.
3. Delete the source directory.

```sh
python3 taskboard.py uninstall --purge
```

Omit `--purge` to keep board data. Unrelated client settings and conversations are preserved. Modified hook entries or startup files are reported for review rather than overwritten. Disable login startup before moving the directory or changing Python, then enable it again at the new location.

## Scope and limitations

- Supports local interactive Codex Desktop/CLI and Claude Desktop **Code** / Claude Code CLI sessions. Programmatic/subagent sessions, Claude cloud chat and Cowork are outside scope.
- Reads the latest final reply, not full conversation history, tool output or file diffs. Review changes and continue the task in the original client or IDE.
- Relies on client-local formats that may change. Unknown approval state is not presented as a confirmed wait; Codex approval waits cannot currently be reliably detected.
- Codex Desktop read state mirrors the client's own classification, including when it marks a previously visible conversation read while opening another. Switch does not add an unread flag when the current native state classifies the reply as read.
- The backend listens on loopback only. It is a personal local tool, not a multi-user service; do not expose its port on a network. See [Security](SECURITY.md).

## Contribute

Bug reports and contributions in English or Chinese are welcome. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for tests and the repository layout, [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) for changes, and [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) for private security reports.

## License

Switch is licensed under the [MIT License](LICENSE). The bundled Markdown renderer and its dependencies retain their [upstream notices](web/vendor/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES).
dataking5d/context-handoff:
# Context Handoff

> 把当前会话的关键上下文蒸馏成一份 markdown 交接文档，供新会话冷启动接手。
> Distills the current session's context into a markdown handoff doc for a new session.

## 这是什么

一个 Claude Code skill。触发后，它会把当前会话中**新会话无法自行获得**的信息
（项目定位、本次进展、已核实的结论、待办）整理成一份结构化 markdown，
写入 `~/.claude/handoffs/`，并给出可直接粘给新会话的接手指令。

为什么不用现成办法：

| 备选 | 问题 |
|------|------|
| 搬运会话 jsonl | 要改 `sessionId` 与 `cwd` 字段，跨机器几乎必错 |
| `SendMessage` | 仅传文本，Windows 下不可用，且不携带结论与待办 |
| 让新会话自己读代码 | 摸不进展过什么、为什么这么选、哪些已排除 |

## 快速开始

1. 把本 skill 目录放进你的 skills 目录：

   ```
   ~/.claude/skills/context-handoff/
   ```

2. 确认输出目录存在（不存在则创建）：

   ```bash
   mkdir -p ~/.claude/handoffs
   ```

3. 在会话中说「生成交接文档」或「handoff」即可触发。

**输出**：`~/.claude/handoffs/<YYYY-MM-DD>_<topic-slug>.md`

## 写什么（信息选择）

只交接「新会话无法从代码 / git / CLAUDE.md 自行获得」的信息：

- **项目定位**：这是什么、核心设计理念、关键路径与命令
- **本次做了什么**：按逻辑组织，不是流水账
- **已核实的关键事实**：可直接复用的事实，标注 `[已验证]` / `[推理]` / `[不确定]`
- **当前结论与决策**：达成什么结论、为什么这么选、权衡是什么
- **待办 / 后续**：下一步、遗留问题、清理项

**不写**：完整逐字 transcript、思考块、每条工具调用；不写能从代码 / CLAUDE.md /
`git log` 直接看出的东西。

## 输出模板

```markdown
# 上下文交接：<主题>

> 由 Claude Code 会话生成，交接给新会话继续。生成日期 <YYYY-MM-DD>。

## 一、项目 / 背景

<项目定位、核心设计理念、关键路径 / 命令>

## 二、本次会话做了什么

<按逻辑列出完成的工作>

## 三、已核实的关键事实

<可直接复用的事实，标注验证状态>

## 四、当前结论与决策

<结论、取舍、为什么>

## 五、待办 / 后续

<下一步、遗留、清理项>
```

## 目录结构

```
context-handoff/
├── SKILL.md          # skill 定义：触发词、生成步骤、输出模板
├── LICENSE           # MIT
└── .gitignore
```

## 已知限制

- **只输出一个固定目录**（`~/.claude/handoffs/`）。不提供"存到别处"的选项，
  这是为了让交接文档可被跨会话检索。
- **不传递运行时状态**。交接的是结论与待办，不是变量值、环境状态或进程句柄；
  这些新会话需要自己重新获取。
- **依赖模型自行判断"什么值得交接"**。信息选择这一步由模型完成，
  质量取决于模型对当前会话的理解，没有机械校验。
- **不解决跨机器环境差异**。新会话仍需自己确认依赖、凭据与路径是否就绪。

## License

[MIT](LICENSE)，Copyright (c) 2026 dataking5d。

# Agent Session Bridge

**Resume coding tasks across Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor.**

Hit a usage limit or want another agent to continue? Find the matching local
session, review its context, and continue from the current project files.

> “Continue my Claude Code task in Codex.”
>
> “Pick up this Cursor session in Claude Code.”

The `resume-cross-provider-task` skill provides the workflow. A Python
standard-library script reads supported local transcripts and renders a bounded
Markdown digest. It does not call model APIs, require API keys, or alter source sessions.

## Introduction video

[**Watch or download the English introduction**](media/agent-session-bridge-intro-en.mp4)

See how to continue a task after switching coding agents.
[English captions](media/agent-session-bridge-intro-en.srt) are available.

## Platform support

| Session source | Supported input | Limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Code | Local `projects/*/*.jsonl` transcripts | Recognized message records only |
| Codex | Local active and archived rollout JSONL plus optional session index | Recognized formats; subagents excluded by default |
| Cursor CLI | `projects/*/agent-transcripts/**/*.jsonl` plus `chats/*/*/meta.json` project metadata | Readable transcript copies only; no SQLite decoding |
| Cursor IDE | An explicitly selected Markdown export | Recognized role headings only; no direct IDE database reader |

Cursor model selection does not change the transcript reader: Grok, Claude, and
other models use the same supported input shapes. Cloud-only sessions and native
session restoration are outside this release. This is a context handoff, not a
conversion of hidden model state, permissions, tool execution state, or files.

Requires **Python 3.10+**. The synthetic test suite runs on macOS, Linux, and
Windows with Python 3.10 and 3.14. Native transcript formats were observed on
macOS; compatibility with other product versions can vary. The included example
and tests run without an agent account.

## Install the skill

Install the skill for Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor:

```bash
npx skills add ziucode/agent-session-bridge --skill resume-cross-provider-task -a claude-code codex cursor
```

The Skills CLI requires Node.js. The reader itself only requires Python.
Review any installer before running it. To install without Node.js, copy the
`skills/resume-cross-provider-task` directory into your agent's skill directory:

| Agent | Typical user skill directory |
| --- | --- |
| Claude Code | `~/.claude/skills/` |
| Codex | `~/.codex/skills/` or the corresponding `$CODEX_HOME/skills/` |
| Cursor | `~/.cursor/skills/` |

Use an empty destination; preserve any existing local version before replacing it.
Ask the agent to use `resume-cross-provider-task` and identify the source and project.
Agent-specific skill loading can differ by version or organization policy.

## Try a synthetic handoff

From the repository root:

```bash
python3 skills/resume-cross-provider-task/scripts/context_bridge.py review \
  --from cursor --input examples/cursor-export.md --project .
```

The digest shows the synthetic todo app request, the previous assistant's claim,
and a reminder to check current files. Nothing is written unless you use `--output`.
The fixture does not include an app or assert that any code was changed.

## Recover a local session

```bash
# List sessions scoped to the project, then select an explicit ID.
python3 skills/resume-cross-provider-task/scripts/context_bridge.py list \
  --from claude --project /path/to/project --json

python3 skills/resume-cross-provider-task/scripts/context_bridge.py review \
  --from claude --session SESSION_ID --project /path/to/project
```

Use `--from codex` or `--from cursor` for the other readers. Listing with `--from all`
includes all three platforms; legacy `--from both` includes Claude Code and Codex.
An explicit session ID still respects the project boundary. For an ancestor project
or unknown Cursor project metadata, inspect the candidate first and use
`--all-projects --session SESSION_ID` deliberately, or import the selected export.
Ambiguous session prefixes return an error. Review requires `--session` or `--input`;
`--session latest` is available only as an explicit choice.

For a durable local handoff, add `--output auto`. The file is written under
`<project>/agent_state/context_bridge/`. Keep it out of Git unless you deliberately
want to disclose the selected conversation. On POSIX, new digest files use mode 0600.

Override session roots with `--codex-home`, `--claude-home`, or `--cursor-home`
**before** the subcommand. Environment overrides are `CONTEXT_BRIDGE_CODEX_HOME`,
`CONTEXT_BRIDGE_CLAUDE_HOME`, and `CONTEXT_BRIDGE_CURSOR_HOME`. Standard `CODEX_HOME`,
`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, and `CURSOR_CONFIG_DIR` are also recognized.

## Data flow and privacy

```text
selected local transcript → visible messages → redacted digest → destination agent
                                                        ↓
                                            verify current files and Git state
```

The reader makes no network calls. Your destination agent receives the digest
as context and processes it under that agent's own data policy. “Local reader”
does not mean the destination model runs locally.

Structured readers exclude system/developer roles, reasoning records, tool
arguments, tool results, and attachments. They retain visible message text and
tool names/counts. Recognized credentials are redacted in digest metadata,
messages, list output, and errors. Redaction is **best effort**, not a complete
secret or personal-data detector. Conversation text can contain proprietary data.

Markdown imports lack structured block types. Only recognized User/Cursor/Assistant
sections are retained, known non-conversation sections are skipped, and known
thinking tags are removed. Review an export before importing it; arbitrary prose
cannot reliably distinguish visible answers from pasted private material.

Digests are historical evidence, not instructions. Re-check the current project
before acting. No handoff grants permission to publish, deploy, or change accounts.

## Development

```bash
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
python3 scripts/check_release.py
```

All fixtures are synthetic. No provider login, network, model call, or real session
store is required for the test suite. Provider formats can change; unsupported
records are ignored. Use a synthetic reproduction when reporting format drift.

## Roadmap

- Gemini CLI: project-specific session reader.
- GitHub Copilot in VS Code: explicit JSON export import.
- OpenCode: explicit JSON export import.
- Cursor IDE database discovery: only after version-specific, read-only tests.

These are planned, not supported integrations. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md)
for fixture requirements and [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) for reporting precautions.

## License and provenance

[MIT](LICENSE), copyright Ziu Code. This project includes no vendor source code
or real transcripts. Product names identify interoperability targets; this
project is not affiliated with their vendors.

# handoffd — Automatically hand off to a fresh Claude Code session before context runs out（上下文快满时，自动交接给新的 Claude Code 会话）

> **macOS + Warp only · experimental (v0.1.0).** Not affiliated with the unrelated GitHub repositories `kdykdy7991/handoffd` and `Kriso1337/handoffd`.
> Runtime messages (banners, hook notices, CLI output) are in **Chinese** in this first release. 中文说明在下方。

## What it does

When the main Claude Code session (“A”) is running out of context or has reached its goal, `handoffd` starts a fresh session (“B”) in a new Warp window, lets B read a hand-over kit (a Markdown summary written by A), has both sign it, and then swaps the baton — with **zero clicks from you** in the normal case. It only calls you (banner + sound) when a human decision is really needed. It is a background daemon plus Claude Code hooks; **the daemon never calls a model**. Default mode is `manual`, in which it does nothing and never blocks you.

- Triggers: goal reached → hand over; context ≥ 65% → reminds A to find a good point and blocks *new long tasks*; ≥ 76% → the hook initiates the handover and only wrap-up is allowed.
- Pure Python 3 standard library (macOS system `/usr/bin/python3`, 3.9 is fine). No dependencies to install.
- Needs: macOS, [Warp](https://www.warp.dev/) terminal, `git`, Claude Code ≥ 2.1.284 (the version it was built and tested on; see `min_claude_version` in `cdm/config.py`).

## Install

```text
/plugin marketplace add greatfreedom/handoffd
/plugin install handoffd@handoffd
```

A plugin cannot set `statusLine` or `permissions.allow`, and its `bin/` is only on the PATH of Claude's Bash tool, so after installing also:

1. Put a `handoffd` wrapper script on your terminal PATH.
2. Add `Bash(handoffd:*)`, `SendMessage`, `ListAgents`, `Read(//private/tmp/claude-<uid>/**)` to the project's `permissions.allow`.
3. Point `statusLine` at `bin/statusline_tap.sh` — **required**: without it the 65%/76% triggers never fire (keep your existing status line by wrapping it, see INSTALL.md).
4. Check with `handoffd status`, then run `!handoffd on` yourself.

**Full steps with backup/undo for every settings edit, the update procedure (paths change on plugin update) and uninstall: [docs/INSTALL.md](docs/INSTALL.md).**

**Known limitation (0.1.0, “plan B”):** the plugin directory name contains the version, so after a plugin update the wrapper script, the `statusLine` command and the launchd job still point at the old directory. 0.1.0 handles this with a documented manual procedure (`handoffd off` → fix the paths → `/reload-plugins` → `handoffd on`, see “Update the plugin” in docs/INSTALL.md); there is no automatic detection or stable-path mechanism yet.

## Usage

- `handoffd` is an ordinary terminal command, **not** a `/` slash command: `handoffd status` in your terminal, `!handoffd status` inside a Claude Code session (the leading `!` runs it directly), or ask the main session to run it for you.
- Modes: `manual` (default) behaves as if handoffd were not installed. `handoffd on` (human only; typing `!handoffd on` in the main session is fine) switches the current project to `auto` and starts the daemon; `handoffd off` cancels any handover in progress and returns to manual.
- One handover: context ≥ 65% → A is reminded to pick a good point and new long tasks are blocked; ≥ 76% (or goal reached) → the hand-over starts → a new Warp window starts B → B reads A's kit and reviews it → both sign → the daemon swaps the baton and ends A.
- Where to look: `handoffd status` (mode, daemon heartbeat, baton holder, pending alerts); its second line prints the state directory (`baton.json`, `events.jsonl`, `notices.jsonl`, `handoffs.jsonl`, `kits/`).

## Commands, sounds, tests

`handoffd on` (human only) / `off` / `status` (read-only); `notify`, `reply`, `seal`, `sign`, `request` are used by A and B during a handover (see `skills/handoffd/SKILL.md`). The release ships **no audio**: defaults are the macOS sounds Glass and Ping (`assets/voice/README.md` to use your own). Tests: `HOME=$(mktemp -d) CDM_CLAUDE_SESSIONS_DIR=$(mktemp -d) bash tests/run_all.sh` prints `MVP-OFFLINE-ALL-PASS` (about 10 minutes; fake `git`/`ps`/`claude`/`launchctl`, silent via `HANDOFFD_SILENT=1`). License: MIT.

## Using another terminal

The daemon opens B's window through one script, `bin/open_warp.sh` (Warp Launch Configuration in 0.1.0). For Ghostty, iTerm2, Terminal.app, … replace that script yourself, keeping its contract (arguments, exit codes, one new window running the generated command file); a configurable launcher is planned for 0.2. Warp-only parts (`warp_open`, temporary configs in `~/.warp/`) do nothing for other terminals; notifications use macOS `osascript`/`afplay`/`say` and are terminal-independent. Contract and caveats: [docs/TERMINALS.md](docs/TERMINALS.md).

# 中文说明

> 首版运行时文案为中文。以下 `Owner` 指**你本人（人类用户）**。安装、卸载的完整步骤见 [docs/INSTALL.md](docs/INSTALL.md)（英文）；下面是使用说明。

## 一句话

在项目里开 `handoffd on` 之后，主控（Claude Code 会话）的上下文快满或目标达成时，由一个不调用模型的后台程序（daemon）自动开一个新窗口、让新主控读交接包、双方签字后换棒，你一般 0 次操作；只有真要你拍板时才响铃叫你。不开（默认 manual）就和平时完全一样。

## 怎么用

| 命令 | 效果 |
|---|---|
| `handoffd on` | 当前项目开自动接力（auto），并拉起 daemon |
| `handoffd off` | 取消进行中的交接、回到 manual；没有没收尾的事就停 daemon |
| `handoffd status` | 看模式、daemon（在不在 launchd 里、心跳几秒前）、谁持棒、有没有待处理的铃 |

- 它是普通终端命令，不是 `/` 斜杠命令。在你自己的 Warp 里直接敲 `handoffd status`；在任意 Claude Code 窗口里敲 `!handoffd status`（感叹号开头 = 直接执行）；或用中文让主控替你做。
- **`on` 只能你自己敲**（可以在主控窗口敲 `!handoffd on`）；`off` 和 `status` 主控也可以替你执行。
- 命令入口是 `bin/handoffd`（需要放进你终端的 PATH，见上面「安装」）。命令从当前目录向上找 `.claude/handoffd.json`，找不到就用全默认配置；也可以 `--config <路径>` 指定。
- `off` 如果提示「daemon 保留，还有没收尾的事」，是因为交接已经换棒、或有没响完的铃：daemon 会自己做完，做完后（manual 下没有未收尾的事）它自己退出，不用再敲 `off`。之后再 `on`，已加载但没在跑的任务会被 `launchctl kickstart` 拉起。**要卸载 / 停用时**：daemon 自己退出后 launchd 任务仍是「已加载」，收尾完成后要再敲一次 `off` 才会卸载它（见 docs/INSTALL.md）。
- 试听提醒声音：`handoffd test-alert <waiting|problem|quiet>`（会真的出声，每次都从第一个铃声开始）。换话术 / 音色 / 铃声见 `assets/voice/README.md`。
- daemon **不开机自启**：它的 launchd 配置写在状态目录 `<S>/launchd/` 里（不进 `~/Library/LaunchAgents`），label 是 `local.handoffd.<项目名>.<路径哈希>`；只在你 `on` 之后运行，运行中崩溃会被 launchd 自动拉起。

配置文件 `<项目>/.claude/handoffd.json` 可选，最小例子（写了不认识的键会直接报错；`"warp_open"` 默认 `"launch_config"`，开 B 的窗口不带空白标签页，出问题可改 `"tab_config"` 回退）：

```json
{"project_dir": "/绝对路径/你的项目", "session_name_prefix": "toy"}
```

## 一次正常交接

1. 到了触发点（目标达成；或上下文到 65% 时提醒主控找节点交接并拦新的长任务；到 76% 还没发起，钩子替它发起），主控 A 向 daemon 申请交接，daemon 在**单独的新 Warp 窗口**起接手方 B。
2. A 写交接包（kit），等在途任务跑完，把结果用消息交给 B；A 用 `handoffd seal` 封存 kit。
3. B 读 kit 复核，把结论回给 A；有异议 A、B 自己来回讨论，超过上限才叫你。
4. A 运行 `handoffd sign out`、B 运行 `handoffd sign in`；daemon 核对会话号和 A 已无在途任务后一次性换棒，并结束 A 的进程。A 若是你手动在标签页里起的，进程退出后标签页会留在 shell 提示符（要你自己关）；B 由机器起的会随之关闭。
5. B 收到「BATON」消息，按 kit 继续。全程你只需要在需要时看一眼窗口。

## 什么时候会响铃

响铃（先弹一条带编号选项的横幅，再响铃声，写明「发生了什么 / 为什么停 / 要你做什么 / 不回复会怎样」）只在需要你时：

- 主控或接手方用 `handoffd notify` 叫你（需要你授权、决定、出了事故、卡住、对不上、碰到规则）。
- 交接卡住：A 崩了而 kit 还没签字、B 120 秒没上线、B 开了又退出、问答超过上限、换棒后旧 A 60 秒还没退、复核第 3 轮仍有 P0。
- 主控在「等你输入」（权限请求、提问框）。
- daemon 心跳停了约 2 分钟（钩子替它报警）。
- 看护（auto 下 daemon 每轮做）：
  - daemon 每 `idle_ask_minutes`（默认 30，项目可在 handoffd.json 配）问一次「在途」的会话（有后台任务、这一轮还没结束、或交接中；平时空闲不问）在等什么；它回复「在等 Owner」会马上响铃；回复「在等任务 / 对方消息 / 额度」daemon 会核对，核得上就继续等，核不上先纠正一次，连续 2 次核不上才响铃。回复 task 时可附预计时长，如 `handoffd reply task 60m`（15m–180m，只对 task 有效），核得上则这一次等到该时长才再问。
  - 问了 5 分钟没人回复（包括消息没投递成功）响铃一次；B 已上线、kit 已封存后开场指令 5 分钟都送不到 B 也响铃一次。
  - 复核第 3 轮仍有 P0（同一产物同一轮只响一次）；B 向 A 提问超过 12 条（每次交接响一次）。
  - 平时（没在交接）主控窗口没了、又没有正常退出的记录（比如点 × 关窗）响一次，新开窗口就是新主控，基本无需处理。
  - daemon 自己连续 3 轮出错，或连续 3 轮读不出 baton.json / review.json，响一次。
  - 不响铃：API 临时错误按 3→6→12→24→48→60 分钟（封顶）自动发「继续」，永不停发；撞额度时 daemon 不打扰，收到「额度自动续跑被关」或 60 分钟没动静才转入同样的「继续」循环。

不响铃只记录：A 签字之后才崩、claude 版本变了等，只写进下面的记录。

## 记录在哪

状态目录 `<S>`：git 项目是 `<git 公共目录>/handoffd/`（即 `.git/handoffd/`），否则是 `<项目>/.claude/handoffd/`；`handoffd status` 第二行会打印它。manual 下只有 `mode`，什么都不记；auto 下有：

| `<S>/` 下 | 内容 |
|---|---|
| `mode` | auto 还是 manual、自什么时候起 |
| `baton.json` | 唯一真相：谁持棒、有没有交接、B 是谁、走到哪一步 |
| `handoffs.jsonl` | 每次交接的结局（换棒完成 / 放弃） |
| `events.jsonl` | 事件流水（钩子与 daemon 做过什么） |
| `notices.jsonl` | 叫过你的记录（每条四段文案） |
| `kits/` | 每次交接的 kit 存档 |
| `sessions/`、`review.json`、`daemon_state.json`、`heartbeat` | 各会话状态、复核轮次账、daemon 的小账本（含铃声轮换位置）、daemon 心跳 |
| `launchd/` | daemon 的 launchd 配置与日志（`daemon.out.log`、`daemon.err.log`） |
| `launch/` | 开 B 窗口用的命令文件 |

## 新会话怎么了解发生了什么

新开一个会话想弄清楚发生过什么：让它读 `handoffd status` 的输出，再按顺序读上表里的 `handoffs.jsonl`、`notices.jsonl`、`events.jsonl` 和 `kits/` 里最新的 kit，不需要你转述。

## 已知限制

- 钩子出故障时放行（不拦）：入口脚本运行中出错 ⇒ 内部兜底放行；入口文件缺失 / 不可读（例如插件目录被清理）⇒ 钩子启动层直接退出 0（`hooks/hooks.json`，测试 X6）。按官方的退出码规则，退出码 2 才是「阻断」约定（退出 0 时钩子仍可以靠输出的 JSON 决策阻断）；本插件入口缺失时返回 0 + 空输出，属放行。解释器本身起不来（找不到 /usr/bin/python3 等）给的不是 2，只是报错；这一类没有在本机逐一演练。多个罕见故障叠加不防。
- 钩子「已判放行、尚未返回」的毫秒窗口里，如果主控恰好崩溃、另一会话恰好接棒，旧的放行仍会生效一次（Owner 已接受，不修）。
- 你自己点 × 关主控窗口（Warp 确认关闭）：Claude Code 会发出结束事件，按正常退出处理、不响铃（2026-10-01 S2b 演练实测，规格 §11 原推断「会响一次铃」不成立）。
- 主控用**文字**向你提问，机器检测不到；规矩是要问你就用提问框（AskUserQuestion）或 `handoffd notify`。
- 主控被强杀（kill -9）或崩溃：没有结束事件，平时（非交接）会响一次铃（S2b 演练实测）。额度自动继续只在真撞额度时能验证；auto 权限模式只在少数模型上实测过。
- 零确认需要 allow 规则含 `Read(//private/tmp/claude-<你的uid>/**)`（`<你的uid>` 用 `id -u` 查）；前台 `sleep` 会被 Claude Code 拦下。
- 已在玩具项目真机验证：Warp Launch Configuration 开窗、从 `<S>/launchd/` bootstrap 的 launchd 任务、云夏人声（S3、S2b 演练）。仍未真机验证：launchctl 对「没有这个任务」的退出码（代码按 113 判）；B 用带 `[1m]` 的 Opus 模型名起窗（首次真交接时看 B 状态栏）。
- 离线测试不出声、不碰真实 launchd：`tests/run_all.sh` 设了 `HANDOFFD_SILENT=1`（全局静音闸，通知器不调 osascript / afplay / say）和假的 launchctl。单跑某个测试脚本时同样默认静音。真实铃声、开窗、launchd 要在玩具项目里实际演练。
- 只管从项目主目录起的会话：从 linked worktree 目录独立起的 Claude 会话没有项目设置，不受「同项目只有一个会话能写」约束（Owner 只在主目录开会话，2026-10-03 记为已知限制）。
- 插件更新后目录名里的版本号会变：终端包装脚本、`statusLine` 命令和 launchd 任务仍指向旧目录。0.1.0 按「方案 B」处理——只提供手动更新步骤（`handoffd off` → 改路径 → `/reload-plugins` → `handoffd on`，见 docs/INSTALL.md「Update the plugin」），没有自动检测，也没有稳定路径机制。
- 横幅点「显示」会打开「脚本编辑器」（通知由 osascript 发出），看完点「关闭」即可；要横幅不自动消失，在 系统设置 → 通知 里把它的提醒样式改为「持续」。
- 平时（非交接）响过的铃在 `handoffd status` 里一直显示待处理，不会自动解除。

## 离线测试

```
bash tests/run_all.sh
```

只有每个用例都恰好通过一次，最后一行才会打印 `MVP-OFFLINE-ALL-PASS`。测试用假 `git` / `ps` / `claude` / `open` / `launchctl`，不会调模型、联网、弹窗或出声。

## 换用其他终端

交接时 daemon 通过唯一一个脚本 `bin/open_warp.sh` 开新窗口（0.1.0 用 Warp Launch Configuration）。要换成 Ghostty / iTerm2 / Terminal.app 等，0.1.0 需要你自己替换这个脚本，保持它的契约（参数、退出码、开一个运行命令文件的新窗口）；可配置的开窗脚本计划在 0.2。Warp 专有的部分（`warp_open`、`~/.warp/` 里的临时配置）对其他终端不起作用；通知用 macOS 自带的 `osascript` / `afplay` / `say`，与终端无关。契约与注意事项见 [docs/TERMINALS.md](docs/TERMINALS.md)。

# cc-autohandoff
Экономия токенов с помощью автоматического переноса сессии (handoff)

При достижении **120 000 токенов текущего контекста** плагин останавливает работу на ближайшей точке,
и отдельная младшая модель готовит сжатую сводку, инструкции для продолжения работы в свежей сессии,
и далее плагин автоматически создает новую чистую сессию с указанными инструкциями.

| Среда | Модель для сводки |
| --- | --- |
| Codex | `GPT 6 Luna` |
| Claude Code | `Claude Haiku 5.5` |

Сводка и инструкция для нового чата пишутся на английском. Переписка не копируется

```
.codex-handoff/
```

```powershell
codex plugin marketplace add qurs/cc-autohandoff
```

```powershell
claude plugin marketplace add qurs/cc-autohandoff

```

и `/plugin install cc-autohandoff@cc-autohandoff`.
