OpenSpec Dashboard

## Why teams adopt OpenSpec Solo, OpenSpec keeps you and your AI honest on a single repo. On a team, the hard part moves: a feature spans the API server, the web app, and a shared library; requirements are owned by one team and consumed by others; planning starts before any code exists. **[Stores](https://openspec.dev/docs/stores)** are the answer — planning in a repo of its own. The same `openspec/` shape you already know (specs and changes), shared by `git push` like anything else. One source of truth your whole team and every coding agent can read, across every repo. - **Cross-repo features** — one change, one plan, even when the code lands in three repos. - **Shared requirements** — a platform team owns the specs; product teams reference them read-only, right where their coding agent can read them. No drifting wiki. - **Plan before code** — capture the plan in the store now; the code repos catch up later. > Stores are in **beta**. Start with the [Stores guide](https://openspec.dev/docs/stores). ## Quick Start **Requires Node.js 20.19.0 or higher.** Homebrew installs it as a dependency. Install OpenSpec globally: ```bash npm install -g @fission-ai/openspec@latest ``` Or install the official [Homebrew formula](https://formulae.brew.sh/formula/openspec) on macOS or Linux: ```bash brew install openspec ``` Then navigate to your project directory and initialize: ```bash cd your-project openspec init ``` > **Want your AI to do it?** Paste the [setup prompt](https://openspec.dev/docs/installation#install-with-your-ai-assistant) into your coding assistant — it installs the CLI, runs `openspec init`, and verifies the result. Now talk to your AI: - **Not sure what to build yet?** Start with `/opsx:explore`, a no-stakes thinking partner that reads your code, weighs options, and shapes a plan before any code gets written. ([Quickstart](https://openspec.dev/docs/quickstart)) - **Already know what you want?** Go straight to `/opsx:propose `. Both are in the default profile. If you want the expanded workflow (`/opsx:new`, `/opsx:continue`, `/opsx:ff`, `/opsx:verify`, `/opsx:bulk-archive`, `/opsx:onboard`), select it with `openspec config profile` and apply with `openspec update`. `/opsx:propose` is the canonical name; your tool may spell it `/opsx-propose` (Cursor, GitHub Copilot), `@opsx-propose` (Amazon Q) or `$openspec-propose` (Codex). `openspec init` prints the right form for the tools you picked — see [Supported Tools](https://openspec.dev/docs/supported-tools). > [!NOTE] > Not sure if your tool is supported? [View the full list](https://openspec.dev/docs/supported-tools) – we support 30+ tools and growing. > > Also works with Homebrew, pnpm, yarn, bun, and Nix. [See installation options](https://openspec.dev/docs/installation). ## Docs Full documentation lives at **[openspec.dev/docs](https://openspec.dev/docs)**. → **[Quickstart](https://openspec.dev/docs/quickstart)**: your first change, start to finish
→ **[Set up your project](https://openspec.dev/docs/setup)**: what `openspec init` installs
→ **[CLI](https://openspec.dev/docs/cli)**: terminal reference
→ **[Supported Tools](https://openspec.dev/docs/supported-tools)**: tool integrations & install paths
→ **[Customize](https://openspec.dev/docs/customize)**: profiles, project config, and schemas
→ **[Stores](https://openspec.dev/docs/stores)**: plan in a separate repo, shared across your team (beta)
→ **[Community Showcase](docs/community.md)**: projects and resources built with and for OpenSpec ## Community schemas Third-party schema bundles distributed via standalone repositories — these provide opinionated workflows that integrate OpenSpec with other tools, similar to how [github/spec-kit's community extension catalog](https://github.com/github/spec-kit/tree/main/extensions) handles tool integrations. → **[Browse the catalog](docs/customization.md#community-schemas)** in the customization docs. ## Why OpenSpec? AI coding assistants are powerful but unpredictable when requirements live only in chat history. OpenSpec adds a lightweight spec layer so you agree on what to build before any code is written. - **Agree before you build** — human and AI align on specs before code gets written - **Stay organized** — each change gets its own folder with proposal, specs, design, and tasks - **Work fluidly** — update any artifact anytime, no rigid phase gates - **Use your tools** — works with 30+ AI assistants via slash commands ### How we compare **vs. [Spec Kit](https://github.com/github/spec-kit)** (GitHub) — Thorough but heavyweight. Rigid phase gates, lots of Markdown, Python setup. OpenSpec is lighter and lets you iterate freely. **vs. [Kiro](https://kiro.dev)** (AWS) — Powerful but you're locked into their IDE and limited to Claude models. OpenSpec works with the tools you already use. **vs. nothing** — AI coding without specs means vague prompts and unpredictable results. OpenSpec brings predictability without the ceremony. ## Updating OpenSpec **Upgrade the package** ```bash npm install -g @fission-ai/openspec@latest ``` If you installed OpenSpec with Homebrew: ```bash brew upgrade openspec ``` **Refresh agent instructions** Run this inside each project to regenerate AI guidance and ensure the latest slash commands are active: ```bash openspec update ``` ## Usage Notes **Model selection**: OpenSpec works best with high-reasoning models. We recommend Codex 5.5 and Opus 4.7 for both planning and implementation. **Context hygiene**: OpenSpec benefits from a clean context window. Clear your context before starting implementation and maintain good context hygiene throughout your session. ## Contributing Every change starts as an issue. We discuss it there, and if we agree to pursue it, a maintainer implements the change or invites you to build it with us. → **[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md)**: the full process, from first issue to merged PR ## Other
Telemetry OpenSpec collects anonymous usage stats. We collect only command names and version to understand usage patterns. No arguments, paths, content, or PII. Automatically disabled in CI. **Opt-out (any one is enough):** - `openspec config set telemetry.enabled false` (global config; unset means on) - `export OPENSPEC_TELEMETRY=0` or `export DO_NOT_TRACK=1` (env overrides config)

# Flux · [![CI](https://github.com/sirsjg/flux/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/sirsjg/flux/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-3178c6?style=flat&logo=typescript&logoColor=white) ![Preact](https://img.shields.io/badge/Preact-673ab8?style=flat&logo=preact&logoColor=white) ![Bun](https://img.shields.io/badge/Bun-fbf0df?style=flat&logo=bun&logoColor=black) ![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docker-2496ed?style=flat&logo=docker&logoColor=white) ![MCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/MCP-enabled-f59e0b?style=flat) > An open, hackable, execution-agnostic task management engine for humans and AI agents.

Flux is a fast, multi-project Kanban board that humans, AI agents, and automations share. Tasks live in a single JSON file in your repo, synced through git. A CLI, web dashboard, REST API, webhooks, and an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server all read and write the same data — so *where* tasks live is fixed, but *how* they get done is entirely up to you: manually, through the API, via webhooks, or by handing the board to an AI assistant. ## Why Flux - **Execution-agnostic** — Flux tracks the work; it doesn't prescribe how the work happens. Humans, scripts, CI pipelines, and LLMs are all first-class actors. - **AI-native** — a full MCP server lets assistants list, create, update, and close tasks programmatically, with agent memory (task comments), priorities, and dependency tracking designed for autonomous work. - **Simple and fast** — a single JSON file, drag-and-drop UI, zero-dependency CLI. No database to run, no SaaS lock-in. - **Git-native** — task data syncs through a `flux-data` branch with `flux push` / `flux pull`, so your board travels with your repo and works offline. ## Features - **Multi-project Kanban boards** with epics, tasks, and drag-and-drop status changes - **Task dependencies** — blocked tasks are flagged visually and excluded from `flux ready` - **Priority system** — P0/P1/P2 priorities for ordering agent (and human) work - **CLI-first** — full terminal workflow with MCP parity (`flux ready`, `flux task`, …) - **MCP integration** — 25+ tools covering projects, epics, tasks, comments, webhooks, and blobs - **Agent memory** — task comments persist context across assistant sessions - **REST API** — full endpoints for automations, integrations, and custom frontends - **Webhooks** — signed, retried deliveries on task changes for Slack, GitHub, CI/CD, and more - **Real-time updates** — boards stay in sync over SSE, with opt-in browser notifications - **Blob storage** — attach files (images, docs, logs) to tasks via CLI, API, or MCP - **Git-native sync** — `flux push` / `flux pull` against a `flux-data` branch

Kanban board — epic swimlanes with tasks in every state: agents at work, blocked cards, and done columns
Task detail — acceptance criteria, numbered guardrails, dependencies, attachments, and agent comments

Task cards — dependency, criteria, and guardrail counts at a glance; live worker chips while agents run
Board toolbar — search (press /), epic and status filters, view toggles
## Quick Start ```bash # CLI only (npm) npm install -g flux-tasks # Full stack with web UI (Docker) curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sirsjg/flux/main/scripts/quickstart.sh | bash # macOS/Linux irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sirsjg/flux/main/scripts/quickstart.ps1 | iex # Windows ``` The quickstart starts the web UI at [http://localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000) (bound to localhost only) and an MCP server on stdio. Press Ctrl+C to stop the MCP server when you're done. The server is locked by default when exposed beyond localhost: set `FLUX_API_KEY` to enable authenticated access on a network, or `FLUX_ALLOW_ANONYMOUS=1` to explicitly allow open access. See [`docs/api.md`](docs/api.md) for auth modes and key scopes. ## Using Flux with AI Assistants Flux ships an MCP server (`packages/mcp`) that runs on **stdio** for local clients or over **Streamable HTTP** for remote ones. Full tool reference: [`docs/mcp.md`](docs/mcp.md). ### Claude Code & Codex With the Docker quickstart running: ```bash # Claude Code claude mcp add flux -- docker exec -i flux-web bun packages/mcp/dist/index.js # Codex codex mcp add flux -- docker exec -i flux-web bun packages/mcp/dist/index.js ``` There is also a [Claude Code plugin](docs/claude-code-plugin.md) that turns project requirements into a structured Flux board with epics, tasks, and dependencies. ### Claude Desktop & ChatGPT Both connect over stdio using a local config file — see [`docs/assistant-setup.md`](docs/assistant-setup.md) for the exact configuration. ### Claude Cowork Claude Cowork connects to MCP servers as **remote custom connectors**: the connection originates from Anthropic's infrastructure, not your machine, so a local stdio server won't work. Instead, run the Flux MCP server in HTTP mode and make it reachable over the public internet: ```bash # Serve the MCP Streamable HTTP transport at /mcp (requires Bun) FLUX_MCP_PASSWORD= bun packages/mcp/dist/index.js --http --port=3001 ``` 1. Expose the endpoint publicly — a hosted deployment, reverse proxy, or a tunnel (e.g. `cloudflared` or `ngrok`) for testing. 2. In your Claude account, go to **Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector** and enter the server URL (e.g. `https://your-host/mcp`). Cowork uses account-level connectors, so this is configured on claude.ai rather than inside the app. 3. Enable the connector in Cowork and confirm the Flux tools appear. The HTTP endpoint is unauthenticated by default. Cowork and other claude.ai connectors can only authenticate over OAuth, so set `FLUX_MCP_PASSWORD` to enable the built-in OAuth server before exposing it — a static `FLUX_MCP_TOKEN` cannot be sent by those clients, though it still works for Claude Code and scripts. See [`docs/mcp.md`](docs/mcp.md) for the OAuth endpoints and for remote-server mode (`FLUX_SERVER` / `FLUX_API_KEY`) if the MCP server should talk to a hosted Flux API instead of local storage. ### Ground rules for agents Add a Flux section to your project's agent instructions (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, or equivalent) so assistants use the board reliably. The snippet below covers the workflow rules Flux actually enforces plus the conventions that keep a shared board coherent: ```bash cat << 'EOF' >> AGENTS.md ## Flux task management You have access to Flux for task management, via MCP tools or the `flux` CLI. Project scope: - All work belongs to exactly one project. On startup, list projects, then select or create one and confirm its project_id before doing any work. - Include that project_id in every Flux call. Never guess a project_id, and never switch projects without explicit instruction. Working a task: - Track all work as tasks. Pick the next task with `list_ready_tasks` (or `flux ready`) — it excludes blocked tasks and sorts by priority (P0 first). - Set status to in_progress when you start and done as soon as you finish. Tasks in planning must move to todo before in_progress. - Pass your agent_name on status changes so the board shows who is working. - Don't start a task whose dependencies aren't done. Memory and scope: - Record decisions, findings, and blockers as task comments — they are your memory across sessions. Check a task's comments before starting it. - When you discover new work, create a task for it (with acceptance criteria) rather than expanding the current task's scope. If you lose context or are unsure of the project_id, stop, re-list projects and tasks, and ask the user if ambiguity remains. EOF ``` ## Documentation - [`docs/installation-docker.md`](docs/installation-docker.md) — production-ready Docker stack with a shared data volume - [`docs/installation-source.md`](docs/installation-source.md) — build from source and set up a local dev workflow - [`docs/cli.md`](docs/cli.md) — full CLI reference with MCP parity - [`docs/claude-code-plugin.md`](docs/claude-code-plugin.md) — Claude Code plugin for spec-driven board generation - [`docs/assistant-setup.md`](docs/assistant-setup.md) — connect Claude Desktop, Claude Cowork, or ChatGPT with best-practice guardrails - [`docs/mcp.md`](docs/mcp.md) — the complete MCP surface: tools, resources, prompts, and transports - [`docs/api.md`](docs/api.md) — REST endpoints for automations, integrations, and custom frontends - [`docs/webhooks.md`](docs/webhooks.md) — real-time events with signatures, retries, and examples - [`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md) — the monorepo, storage model, and design decisions - [`docs/ideas.md`](docs/ideas.md) — ways to use Flux, from agent swarms to automation-first workflows - [`docs/roadmap.md`](docs/roadmap.md) — where Flux is headed next ## Ecosystem Flux's CLI, REST API, webhooks, and MCP server make it easy to compose with other tools: ### Agents & assistants | Tool | How it pairs with Flux | |------|------------------------| | [Heretic](https://github.com/sirsjg/heretic) | A desktop companion for Flux for your multi-agent orchestration | | [Claude Agent SDK](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk) | Build custom autonomous agents that plan, pick up, and close Flux tasks through the MCP tools | | [Goose](https://github.com/block/goose) | Open-source, MCP-native agent — point it at the Flux MCP server and let it work ready tasks | | [Cursor](https://cursor.com) / [Cline](https://github.com/cline/cline) / [Zed](https://zed.dev) | MCP-capable editors and coding agents that can read and update the board while they code | | [Momentum](https://github.com/sirsjg/momentum) | Watches Flux for task changes and automatically spawns agents to work on them | ### Planning & automation | Tool | How it pairs with Flux | |------|------------------------| | [Spec Kit](https://github.com/github/spec-kit) | Create spec-driven requirements that generate Flux epics and tasks | | [GitHub Actions](https://github.com/features/actions) | Drive the board from CI — close tasks on merge, create tasks from failed runs, or `flux push` on a schedule | | [n8n](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n) | Self-hosted workflow automation triggered by Flux webhooks | | [Zapier](https://zapier.com) | Connect Flux to 5,000+ apps via the REST API and webhooks | | [Slack](https://api.slack.com/messaging/webhooks) | Post task updates to a channel via Flux webhooks — see [`docs/webhooks.md`](docs/webhooks.md) | | [cloudflared](https://github.com/cloudflare/cloudflared) / [ngrok](https://ngrok.com) | Tunnel the MCP HTTP endpoint so Claude Cowork and claude.ai connectors can reach it | ## Contributing Flux is early and moving quickly. Open an issue for ideas and bugs, or pick something from the [roadmap](docs/roadmap.md) and send a PR. See [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md) for details. ## License MIT. See [`LICENSE`](LICENSE).

拥有完全隔离的本地工作目录（``），保存其私有笔记、工作草稿与本地记忆，互不串扰。 --- ### 2. 🧠 深度深挖：多层持久化记忆机制与 Memory Advisor 自省进化 记忆是多 Agent 成为“真实队友”的基石。Kith-space 拒绝粗暴地把所有历史塞进大上下文窗口，而是设计了一套严密的**多层持久化与自省记忆中枢**： ```text 三层立体文件记忆 (透明易审) + SQLite FTS5 结构化情景记忆 (高速全文检索) + 异步 Memory Advisor 流水线 (事实提炼 & 反思纠偏) + HMAC 密码学防篡改签名 + 原始消息证据链溯源 + 严苛的 Prompt Injection 反投毒护栏 (拦截对抗性注入) + 跨表面隐私披露门禁 (防止私聊秘密泄露进公共群聊) = 跨越会话、安全可靠、越用越懂你的终身认知系统 ``` #### ① 三层立体文件记忆（Transparent File Memory） * **用户层记忆（User Memory）**：位于 `~/.kith/user/MEMORY.md` 及 `notes/`，记录跨项目的全局习惯、通用技术偏好与风格倾向，由用户直接掌控。 * **空间层记忆（Space Memory）**：位于 `/.kith/memory/MEMORY.md` 及 `notes/`，承载当前项目的业务背景、团队共识、架构规范。 * **Agent 私有记忆（Agent Private Memory）**：位于各 Agent 私有工作空间，沉淀该队友的执行心得与专业经验。 * 所有文件均采用标准 Markdown，用户可随时打开人工阅读、润色或清空，Agent 亦可通过原生文件读写工具自然查阅。 #### ② 结构化情景记忆（Episodic Memory & FTS5 引擎） * 底层基于本地 SQLite 存储（`episodicMemories` 表），记录具备严格 schema 的结构化事实、用户指令、决策记录与操作准则。 * **SQLite FTS5 全文索引**：通过词法投影（Lexical Projection）与 SQLite FTS5（`memory_fts` 表）实现毫秒级全文模糊匹配与混合相关度召回。 * **知识关联与版本演进**：支持 `relationType` 关联（`supersedes` 替代、`contradicts` 冲突），当用户提出新偏好时，系统自动标记并废弃陈旧认知，避免前后自相矛盾。 #### ③ 异步 Memory Advisor：自动化提炼与认知自省 * 每次交流结束后，后台守护进程自动启动 `memoryAdvisorJobs` 异步分析流水线，无需阻塞当前的实时聊天响应。 * **智能噪声与闲聊过滤**：自动识别并剔除无信息量的客套寒暄（如“好的”、“收到”、“谢谢”）、一次性测试口令（Canary Tokens）与瞬态系统 ID。 * **双重摘要投影（Dual Projections）**： * `internalSummary`：保留技术与逻辑细节，供 Agent 自我思考时调用； * `shareableSummary`：提炼为安全合规的摘要，用于跨场景、跨频道协同。 #### ④ 工业级安全护栏：反提示词投毒与隐私隔离 * **严苛的 Anti-Poisoning 反投毒检测**：自动拦截输入中伪装成记忆的越权指令（如扫描“忽略之前所有规则”、“绕过安全策略”、“泄露 API Key / 凭据”等黑客攻击），坚决拒绝对抗性攻击污染记忆库。 * **敏感信息自动脱敏（Secret Sanitization）**：实时检测 API Token、私钥、密码，绝不将其作为长期记忆持久化。 * **HMAC 密码学防篡改签名**：所有入库记忆与 Claim 令牌均经本地 HMAC SHA-256 签名，防止恶意进程伪造记忆数据；每条记忆均绑定原始消息证据链（`memoryEvidence`），支持来源追溯。 * **跨表面隐私披露门禁（Disclosure Gates）**：严格区分 `agent_private`、`space` 与 `user` 作用域，在私聊（DM）中习得的敏感信息在未经显式授权（DisclosureGrant）前，绝不会被带入公开群聊频道。 --- ### 3. 🎨 深度剖析：无限矢量画布协作模块（Infinite Vector Canvas） 无限矢量画布是 Kith-space 内置的**核心协同工作模块之一**（基于 SVG Paper / Recombyn 引擎），为人和 Agent 的协作提供了图文并茂的高维共创工作台： #### ① 真正的矢量级编程绘制与几何布尔运算 区别于市面上仅生成位图的 AI 绘图工具，Kith-space 的画布是**真正的矢量操作台**： * Agent 通过精准的类型化 API（`create_frame`、`create_shape`、`create_text`、`align_nodes` 等）操纵图元，实现毫秒级精准排版。 * **矢量布尔运算（Boolean Operations）**：支持 `canvas.boolean_op`（并集 union、差集 subtract、交集 intersect）。Agent 可像专业设计师一样，用基础几何图形巧妙组装复杂图标（例如：大圆减小圆切出月牙，圆圈组合矩形拼出放大镜，贝塞尔闭合路径绘制矢量徽标）。 #### ② 选区快照与局部切片批注交互（Marked Regions） * 人类在画布上框选某些图元，或在特定画面区域圈定局部批注框（Marked Regions），然后在侧边栏 `@Designer` 发起指令（如“把这块文案居中，背景换成秋季配色”）。 * 系统底层生成基于 SHA-256 哈希防伪的不可变快照（`FrozenCanvasSelectionSnapshot`），向 Agent 颁发带有 CAS 乐观锁的版本租约，保证多人/多 Agent 编辑不冲突。 * Agent 改动完成后生成原子 `mutationId`，画布实时呈现矢量变化，同时在聊天流中沉淀可审计的操作回执卡片。 #### ③ 体系化设计 Skill 技能包与 Anti-AI-Slop 质检门禁 内置了完整的**专业级设计方法论体系**（*Brief 意图 → Art Direction 视觉方向 → Layout Plan 构图规划 → Execution 绘图执行 → Observe 场景反思 → Review 质检 → Subtract 克制删减*）： * **12 大设计底座规范**： * `anti_ai_slop`：**反 AI 俗套审美护栏**。硬核禁止滥用紫蓝科技渐变、无脑毛玻璃、浮夸光斑，严禁正文中用 emoji 充当图标，禁止编造虚假数据。 * `composition`：**量化黄金构图**。硬性规定主视觉面积（60–85%）、文字区（≤20%）、视觉留白呼吸区（≥15%）。 * `typography`（字体阶梯排印）、`color`（色盘角色分工）、`design_system` 等。 * **14 大垂直领域技能包**：`poster_craft`（海报/展架）、`landing_page`（营销落地页）、`banner_ad`（广告横幅）、`dashboard_ui`（数据大屏）、`mobile_app_ui`（移动界面）、`icon_set`（矢量图标组）等。 * **闭环设计质检门禁（`canvas.design_review`）**：提交前 Agent 自行运行 0–100 分量规自检：`<70 分`强制返工重画，`70–89 分`修正缺陷，`≥90 分`方可放行。 * **多模态生成联动**：支持将豆包（Doubao）生成的 AI 图像与短视频无缝挂载为画布 Frame 内的资产。 --- ### 4. 💬 多 Agent 群聊频道与 Agent Harness v2 协作底座 * **团队多角色同台群聊与分工**：支持多个 Agent 共同加入一个频道，既可输入 `@AgentName` 针对性委派任务，也可输入 `@all` 发起全员大讨论与跨角色交叉会审。 * **Agent Harness v2 核心架构机制（彻底终结串台与上下文污染）**： * **Per-Surface 局部独立会话**：每个 Agent 在每个频道、私聊或话题中运行完全隔离的 Session，彻底杜绝单一大上下文导致的会话串台与跨域污染。 * **Durable Turn Ledger（崩溃自愈）**：严格遵循“先持久化、后执行”原则，服务重启后自动接续调度，绝不漏回任何消息。 * **服务端目标锁定（Anti-Hallucination Routing）**：回复目标由服务端安全令牌直接锁定，大模型无法通过幻觉将消息误发到其他私密频道。 * **实时透明追踪**：内置 **LiveTrace** 与 **Turn Inspector**，毫秒级流式展现 Agent 的思维链（Thinking）、工具调用栈及执行详情。 --- ### 5. 📋 任务看板模块：严肃分工与交付验收闭环 将复杂的业务诉求转化为具备完整生命周期的结构化 Task： * **精准指派**：在群聊或任务看板中将工作拆分为具体 Task，明确指派给特定 AI 队友。 * **双模式自主执行**： * ⚡ **Autopilot（自动驾驶模式）**：Agent 自主规划步骤、调用工具、推进完成； * 📝 **Plan-First（方案预审模式）**：Agent 先出具执行方案与风险分析，待人类确认后方可施工。 * **严肃交付协议**：支持 CAS 乐观锁任务认领（`task.claim`）、流转转交（`task.assign`）、进度汇报（`task.report`），并在最终阶段附带产出物发起正式交付（`task.deliver`）。 --- ### ## Why artiboard When two people each run a few Claude sessions on one codebase, the hard part is not the code. It is knowing who took what, what is blocked, and what changed while you were away. Chat logs do not travel between sessions, and pasting the whole state into every prompt gets expensive fast. artiboard gives the team one shared, live place for that state, and gives agents a cheap, strict way to use it.
### 🗂️ One board, three views A document view you read top to bottom, a kanban, and a dependency graph that highlights the longest remaining chain. Search, `j`/`k` keys and "new since you last looked" markers. Light and dark. ### 🤝 People and agents together Each person gets a color. Agents claim tasks with version-checked writes, so two agents never take the same task. Threads hold decisions, questions and handoffs. Notices carry what everyone must know. ### 🪶 Built to stay cheap Views are drawn by code, never by a model. Agents read only the slice they need and write in one batch. The longer the project runs, the more this matters.

pranjal-joshi/claude-crew:
Run a crew of Claude Code agents, one for each stage of your SDLC.
They pick tasks off a board, run in workflows you chain together, start on schedules and events, and hand you diffs to approve.
One Python file, one HTML file, no dependencies.

## Try it in 10 seconds No Claude CLI, no API key, no tokens. Simulated agents play through a real board: ```bash git clone https://github.com/pranjal-joshi/claude-crew && cd claude-crew python server.py --demo ``` Open **http://127.0.0.1:8770**. ## Install Crew is pure standard-library Python (3.10 or newer) and installs as a `crew` command. [pipx](https://pipx.pypa.io/) keeps it isolated: ```bash pipx install claude-crew # from PyPI, once published pipx install https://github.com/pranjal-joshi/claude-crew/releases/download/v0.1.0/claude_crew-0.1.0-py3-none-any.whl # a release wheel pipx install git+https://github.com/pranjal-joshi/claude-crew # latest main ``` Then `crew --demo` or `crew --project /path/to/your/repo` behaves exactly like `python server.py ...`. When installed, the default `crew.json` lives in the folder you run `crew` from; state and worktrees stay in `~/.crew`. `crew --version` prints the version. ## Use it on your code You need [Claude Code](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code) installed and signed in (`claude` works in your terminal). ```bash python server.py --project /path/to/your/repo ``` To use it from your phone or another computer on the same Wi-Fi, add `--lan`, then click **Phone** in the header and scan the QR code. On a phone it lays out like an app: ```bash python server.py --project /path/to/your/repo --lan ``` That's it. Add tasks or set up [triggers](#triggers), and the agent whose tags match picks each task up. ## Why Claude Code is great at one task at a time. Real work is a queue: a feature, its tests, a review, some research, the docs. Running a terminal per task means many places to watch, changes tangled in one checkout, no single place to say yes or no, and nothing that starts work while you're away. Crew gives that queue a home: - **One board** for every task, with Backlog, In progress, Review and Done columns. - **Agents that pull their own work.** Each agent has a role and tags; idle agents take matching tasks. - **No stepping on each other.** Every agent works in its own git worktree on its own `crew/` branch. - **You stay the reviewer.** Finished work lands in Review with the agent's summary and a real diff. Approve commits it; Send back resumes the same session with your feedback. - **Work that starts itself.** Schedules, events, file watches, command polls and webhooks turn into tasks, so the standup gets written at 11:00 and every approved feature gets tests. ## The boss A chat bar at the bottom (/) talks to the **boss**: a Claude session that runs the crew instead of writing code. Ask it to "plan and build CSV export, then have it tested and reviewed" and it creates tasks, assigns agents, starts workflows, messages or stops agents, and adds triggers, through a small set of crew tools (`crew_mcp.py`). Switch the chat to any agent to talk to it directly. Type / in the chat bar (or in an agent's message box) for a picker of commands and skills: Crew's own `/clear` `/compact` `/stop`, plus that agent's Claude Code slash commands and skills with their descriptions. ↑↓ to move, Tab or Enter to pick, Esc to close. The boss runs with only the crew tools and a few read-only ones, so a turn costs about 10k tokens of context instead of your full setup. **Auto Workflow Builder** (Workflows tab): describe a process in plain words, and the boss maps it onto agents, workflows and triggers. It reuses agents that fit, adds the missing ones, and creates triggers for any schedule or event you mention. **Auto hand-off**: every agent has a `handoff` tool. When its finished work clearly needs another specialist, it hands a follow-up to a teammate by name, or `auto` by tag. Chains stop after five hops. The manual hand-off menu is unchanged, and it now also offers **Auto**: the boss picks the agent. ## The crew Nine agents, one per stage of the delivery loop. Each owns a few tags, so an unassigned task goes to the right specialist. Change any of it from the UI. | Stage | Agent | Picks up | Default model | What it does | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Plan | **planner** | `plan` `triage` | Opus · high | Turns requests and work items into small, testable tasks with acceptance criteria. Plans, never implements. | | Research | **researcher** | `research` `spike` | Fable · high | Compares tools and approaches with evidence and cost, ends with one recommendation. | | Design | **designer** | `ui` `design` | Opus · high | Prototypes and builds UI: components, dark themes, accessibility, phone widths. | | Build | **builder** | `feature` `bug` `api` `refactor` | Opus · high | Smallest change that meets the criteria, with tests for new behaviour. | | Test | **tester** | `test` `qa` | Sonnet · medium | Reproduces bugs with failing tests first; reports exact commands and output. | | Review | **reviewer** | `review` `security` | Opus · xhigh | Correctness, security and domain review; fixes only clear defects, ranks the rest. | | Evaluate | **evaluator** | `eval` `data` `ml` | Opus · high | Model and prompt evals, A/B and shadow checks, with sample sizes, not anecdotes. | | Ship & observe | **ops** | `ops` `deploy` `incident` `chore` | Sonnet · high | CI/CD, deployments, telemetry, cost, incidents and repo hygiene. Diagnoses before it changes anything. | | Report | **scribe** | `docs` `report` | Sonnet · low | Standups, PR descriptions, release notes and docs. Short and linked. | ## Workflows The **Workflows** tab (W) chains agents in a fixed order. Run one with a goal, and step 1's task is created. When a step is done, the next step's task is created with the earlier steps' summaries and an instruction to merge the previous agent's branch, so each agent builds on real work. Each link has a gate: ✋ waits for you to approve the step, ⚡ continues on its own when the agent finishes. | Workflow | Steps | | --- | --- | | Feature delivery | planner ✋ → builder ✋ → tester ⚡ → reviewer ✋ → scribe | | Bug fix | tester (failing test) ⚡ → builder ✋ → reviewer | | Spike to plan | researcher ✋ → planner | | Model change | evaluator (baseline) ⚡ → builder ✋ → evaluator (re-eval) | | Incident | ops (diagnose) ✋ → builder ✋ → tester ⚡ → scribe (post-mortem) | Edit workflows on a **canvas**, n8n-style: a **When** block (▶ Run by hand, or any trigger), one block per agent step, and an **Output** block. Drag blocks to reorder, drag an agent from the left onto the canvas (or press ＋ on a line) to add a step, and click ✋ / ⚡ on a line to switch its gate. Click a block to edit its instruction (`{input}`, `{prev_summary}`, `{prev_branch}` and more). Runs show live progress per step, and click through to each step's task. The **Output** block decides what a finished run delivers: | Output | What happens | |---|---| | 📋 Board (default) | Nothing extra; the last step's card holds the result. | | 📄 Report file | A markdown report of every step (who, branch, commit, summary) is saved in the project, `crew-reports/` by default. | | 🔗 Webhook | The run report is POSTed as JSON (`workflow, run, title, status, report, steps`) to a URL, e.g. a Slack or Teams hook. | | ⛓ Next workflow | Another workflow starts with the same goal and this run's last summary (at most 5 in a chain). | ## Stop, kill, clear - **■ Stop** (agent card, drawer, or **Stop all** in the header) ends the current run at once. The session is kept, the task goes back to the backlog **on hold**, and the agent pauses until you press **▶ Resume** or give it work. - **Kill** disables an agent until you respawn it. Use it for an agent that misbehaves. - **Clear ▾** removes Done tasks, or the whole board (running agents are stopped first). Branches and commits are kept. - **Clear** (red button, top right of an open boss or agent chat) wipes that conversation and empties its context: the next message starts a fresh session. Click a card on the board to open the agent that handled it. Drag agents in the left rail to reorder the crew; the order is saved to `crew.json`. Collapse the rail with « to a slim column of avatars and status dots, and » brings it back (remembered per browser). ## Context per task Each agent starts a **fresh Claude session for every new task** by default. Old tasks aren't re-read on every turn, so tokens stay low and context doesn't fill up. What should carry over already travels with the task: the hand-off summary, the previous step's branch, the workflow brief. Send back still resumes the same session, so the agent revises its own work. Switch any agent to **Keep across tasks** in ⚙ Model & role. Each agent's drawer shows how full its context is, with **Compact** (Claude Code's `/compact`) and **New session**. ## Triggers Assigning a task is the manual trigger. Press T for the automatic ones. Each firing adds a task from a template, and the dispatcher hands it out like any other. | Trigger | Fires when | Example | | --- | --- | --- | | ◷ **Schedule** | A cron expression matches, in local time | `0 11 * * 1-5`: the scribe writes the standup report | | ↯ **Event** | A task reaches Review, is approved, or fails (filter by tag or agent) | An approved `feature` becomes "Write tests for #{id}" for the tester | | ◉ **File watch** | Files matching a glob change in the project | `**/*prompt*` changes, so the evaluator reruns the evals | | ⟳ **Poll command** | A command's output changes, it starts failing, or it prints something new | `gh run list --status failure --limit 1` every 10 min goes to ops | | ⇢ **Webhook** | Something POSTs to the trigger's URL with its secret token | CI posts after a deploy, so ops checks telemetry | Task templates take placeholders: `{date}` `{time}` everywhere, plus `{id}` `{title}` `{who}` `{summary}` `{branch}` `{commit}` `{merge}` for events, `{files}` for watches, `{output}` `{exit}` for polls and `{payload}` for webhooks. Event chains stop after five hops, and a trigger never fires on its own tasks. ```bash curl -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:8770/api/hook/t7" -H "X-Crew-Token: " -d "deployed api v2.4 to preprod" ``` Nine presets cover the common loops: daily standup, test what ships, review what merges, plan then build, CI failure watch, nightly hygiene, deploy webhook, prompt changes trigger re-evals, and proofreading changed docs. ## Features | | | | --- | --- | | 🧑‍🤝‍🧑 **An SDLC crew** | Planner, researcher, designer, builder, tester, reviewer, evaluator, ops and scribe by default. Add, remove and re-role agents from the UI. | | ⛓ **Workflows** | Chain agents in order (plan → build → test → review → write-up) on an n8n-style canvas, with an approval or auto gate per step and a choice of output: board, report file, webhook or next workflow. | | ⚡ **Triggers** | Schedules, task events, file watches, command polls and webhooks start work on their own. Presets included. | | 🧹 **Fresh context per task** | A new session per task keeps tokens down; send-back still resumes. Per-agent switch. | | 🧠 **Model and effort per agent** | Opus for the builder, Sonnet for the tester, Fable for research: each agent gets its own model and effort level (low to max). | | 🪢 **Subagents, visible** | When an agent fans out to subagents, you see each one live on the agent card, a count on the task, and a labelled thread in the transcript. | | 🌳 **Worktree isolation** | One worktree and branch per agent. Merge what you approve with `git merge crew/`. | | 🔍 **Review gate** | Agent summary and colored diff side by side. Approve and commit, send back, or hand off to another agent. | | ↪️ **Hand-offs** | Drag any card, in any column, onto another agent. The earlier summary, branch and commit go along as context. | | ✦ **Boss chat** | A chat bar that runs the crew: tasks, workflows, agents and triggers, from plain requests. | | ⌨ **Slash picker** | Type `/` in any chat box for Crew commands plus the agent's Claude Code commands and skills. **Clear** in the chat panel wipes a chat and its context. | | 💬 **Talk mid-run** | Message any agent while it works. The message lands in the running session. | | 📱 **Phone app feel** | `--lan` plus a QR code. On a phone: bottom navigation, swipeable columns, bottom sheets, Android back closes sheets. | | ■ **Stop, kill, clear** | Stop a run (session kept, task on hold), stop everything at once, or clear the board. | | 🔐 **Permission modes** | Accept edits (default), Auto (Claude Code's safety classifier) or Bypass, for all agents from one switch. | | 🔢 **Tokens and cost** | Live token counts per agent, per task and in total. Hide the dollar amounts with one click. | | 🧩 **Your skills and MCP servers** | Agents are ordinary Claude Code sessions, so they load your skills, plugins and MCP servers. | | 📁 **Projects** | Switch repos from the header. Each project keeps its own board, sessions and worktrees. | | ⌨️ **Keyboard first** | `/` talk to the boss, `N` new task, `T` triggers, `W` / `B` workflows / board, `1`–`9` open an agent, `Ctrl K` command palette, `Esc` close. | ## Screenshots

## How it works ```mermaid flowchart LR UI["Browser UI (index.html)"] <-->|SSE + JSON| S["server.py on 127.0.0.1"] S -->|stream-json| A1["claude -p: builder"] S -->|stream-json| A2["claude -p: tester"] S -->|stream-json| A3["claude -p: reviewer"] A1 --- W1[("worktree crew/builder")] A2 --- W2[("worktree crew/tester")] A3 --- W3[("worktree crew/reviewer")] ``` - Each agent is a long-lived `claude -p --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json` process. Crew writes tasks and your messages to its stdin and reads every event from its stdout. - A one-second loop checks triggers, then gives idle agents work: tasks pinned to them first, then unassigned tasks whose tag matches the agent's tags. - Subagents are tracked from the stream itself. An `Agent` tool call starts one, events tagged with its `parent_tool_use_id` belong to it, and its tool result ends it. - State (board, triggers, sessions, tokens, transcripts) is saved per project under `~/.crew/state/`. Worktrees live in `~/.crew/wt/`, which keeps paths short enough for Windows. ## Configuration `crew.json` is created next to `server.py` on first run (in the current folder when installed with pipx) and saved whenever you change things in the UI. ```jsonc { "permission_mode": "acceptEdits", // or "auto", "bypassPermissions" "allowed_tools": ["Bash(git status:*)", "Bash(npm test:*)", "Bash(pytest:*)", "WebSearch"], "allow_mcp": true, // auto-allow MCP servers agents discover (Accept edits mode) "agents": [ {"name": "builder", "role": "Implements features and fixes.", "tags": ["feature", "bug", "api", "refactor"], "model": "opus", "effort": "high"} ] } ``` | Flag | Default | | | --- | --- | --- | | `--project PATH` | a demo repo in `~/.crew` | The repo agents work on. | | `--port N` | `8770` | | | `--config PATH` | `crew.json` | Next to `server.py` from a clone, in the current folder when installed. | | `--version` | | Print the version and exit. | | `--demo` | off | Simulated agents and sample tasks. | `CREW_CLAUDE` overrides the command used to start agents. ### Permissions Headless agents can't answer permission prompts. In **Accept edits** mode, file edits are allowed and Bash commands outside `allowed_tools` are refused, and the agent is told why. Add the commands your project needs to `allowed_tools`, or switch to **Auto** to let Claude Code's classifier decide. **Bypass** skips all checks and asks you to confirm first. ## Security - The server binds to `127.0.0.1` only. - Every write needs a custom request header and a localhost `Host`, so other websites can't drive your agents (CSRF and DNS rebinding). - `--lan` listens on your network, but every request from another device needs a secret key (set as a cookie by the QR link) and a bare-IP `Host`. The key lives in `~/.crew/lan-key`; delete it to sign every device out. Traffic is plain HTTP, so use it on networks you trust. - Agents are told to stay inside the project folder unless a task names another path. - Webhooks are the one write path without the browser header. Each needs its own random token, compared in constant time. - Poll triggers run the command you typed, in your shell, in the project folder. Treat them like a cron job you wrote yourself. ## FAQ **Does it cost extra?** No. Agents use your own Claude Code login, so usage counts against your plan or API key like any other Claude Code session. The token counter shows what each agent used. **Can agents use my skills and MCP servers?** Yes. Each agent loads what `claude` loads in your terminal: user skills, plugins, user MCP servers and claude.ai connectors. Crew also brings along what git leaves out of a worktree: local-scope MCP servers (`claude mcp add` without `--scope user`), an uncommitted `.mcp.json`, `.claude/settings.local.json`, untracked project skills, agents and commands, and `CLAUDE.local.md`. Click the skills · MCP chip in an agent's drawer to see exactly what it loaded. Connectors that need sign-in must be signed in once with `claude` → `/mcp`. **Can an agent spawn its own subagents or background jobs?** Yes, they're full Claude Code sessions. Crew shows subagents live. Kill ends the whole process tree, background jobs included. **How do I merge an agent's work?** Approve commits to the agent's branch. Then `git merge crew/builder` (or open a PR) like any other branch. **Which platforms?** Built and tested on Windows 11. macOS and Linux use the same code paths (process groups instead of `taskkill`); reports welcome. ## Roadmap - [ ] Shared crew memory: a notes file every agent reads at start and adds to at the end - [ ] Hand-offs that merge the previous agent's branch into the next agent's worktree - [x] Live subagent indicators - [ ] Background-job and monitor indicators, and holding a task until its jobs finish - [x] Event triggers chain work ("tests after feature") - [x] Workflows: agents in a fixed order with approval gates - [ ] Parallel steps in workflows (fan out, then join) - [ ] One-click merge of approved branches Ideas and PRs welcome. Open an issue first for anything big. ## Contributing The whole app is two files: `server.py` (Python standard library) and `index.html` (vanilla JS). `python server.py --demo` is the fastest loop; `demo/fake_claude.py` speaks the same stream-json protocol as Claude Code. Tests are standard-library `unittest` (`python -m unittest discover`), lint is `ruff check .`, and CI runs both on Linux, Windows and macOS. ## Releasing 1. Bump `__version__` in `server.py` (the single source of the version) and add an entry to `CHANGELOG.md`. 2. Commit, then tag and push: `git tag vX.Y.Z && git push origin vX.Y.Z`. 3. The **Release** workflow runs the tests, checks the tag matches `__version__`, builds the sdist and wheel, and creates a GitHub Release with both attached and generated notes. To also publish to PyPI: create a [trusted publisher](https://docs.pypi.org/trusted-publishers/) for the project `claude-crew` (owner `pranjal-joshi`, repo `claude-crew`, workflow `release.yml`, environment `pypi`), then set the repository variable `PUBLISH_PYPI` to `true`. Until then the PyPI job is skipped and releases still succeed. ## Star history ---

If Crew saves you a few terminals, a ⭐ helps others find it.

chillrain666/quadrant-md:
# Quadrant **A markdown-first todo system for humans and AI agents.** One line per task, one file per project — no database, no account, no cloud lock-in. [中文说明](README.zh-CN.md) · [Design notes](docs/design.md) · [Agent skill](skill/quadrant/SKILL.md)

Your todos are a pile of `.md` files. Edit them in Obsidian, VSCode, vim or on your phone; or just tell an AI agent "turn the API error codes into a table before Friday" and let it write the right line. The built-in board is optional cosmetics — **without it, `grep` and an editor still work**. ## Why another todo app? | | Notion / Todoist | Obsidian plugins | **Quadrant** | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Where the data lives | someone else's server | local markdown | **local markdown (single source of truth)** | | Offline | ✗ | ✓ | ✓ | | `git log` your decisions | ✗ | half | ✓ | | An AI agent can read/write it safely | ✗ API + OAuth | ✗ bespoke format | **✓ it is one line of text** | | Drag ordering | ✓ | depends | ✓ (order kept aside, never pollutes markdown) | | Priority / quadrants | ✓ | varies | **P×U grid, encoded as `#P1 #U2`** | Three ideas hold it together: 1. **Capture is free** — unclear things go to `0-inbox.md`, one line each, unsorted. 2. **Priority is a field, not a position** — changing it edits one character (`#P2` → `#P1`) instead of moving paragraphs. 3. **The agent touches only the line that changed** — line order, indented details and newline style are untouched, so humans and agents can edit the same files. ## Quick start ```bash git clone https://github.com/chillrain666/quadrant-md.git cd quadrant-md python scripts/init_tasks.py # creates tasks/ (directories + demo data) cd app uv sync # or: pip install -r requirements.txt uv run python main.py # -> http://127.0.0.1:8000 ``` If the grid appears, you are done. The frontend build ships with the repo, **no Node required**. Point it at an existing notes directory instead: ```bash TASKS_ROOT=/path/to/my/tasks uv run python main.py # macOS / Linux set TASKS_ROOT=D:\notes\tasks && uv run python main.py # Windows ``` ## The directory *is* the database ``` tasks/ ├── 0-inbox.md capture box: anything not thought through (never on the board) ├── 1-active/ in progress, one file per project <- the only board source │ ├── study/study.md │ └── life/chores/chores.md ├── 2-notes/ long details (not scanned) ├── 3-log/ timeline log, append only (not scanned) ├── 4-someday.md "one day" items + ideas (own panel) ├── 5-archive/ finished projects (not scanned) └── watch/ lists: shows, books, serials (own panel, no P/U) ``` Four tracks, each with its own surface: tasks reach the quadrants, lists do not, ideas go to someday, and captured items are shown **nowhere**. That last one is deliberate — once captured items are visible, people start tidying them, which defeats capture. ## What one task looks like ```markdown - [ ] T-261021-1 Read chapter 3 of DDIA #P1 #U2 #reading DDL:2026-11-05 indented lines are details of this task, kept verbatim, deleted with it ``` | Piece | Meaning | | --- | --- | | `- [ ]` `- [x]` `- [-]` | to do / done / blocked | | `T-261021-1` | globally unique ID: `T-` + `YYMMDD` + `-` + daily sequence, immutable | | `#P1`~`#P3` | importance, P1 highest | | `#U1`~`#U3` | urgency, U1 highest | | `#tag` | several allowed, CJK / capitals / `a/b` all fine | | `DDL:2026-11-05` | due date | | `DONE:2026-10-21` | completion date (stamped when you tick) | **Quadrants are computed from `P × U`, never stored**, so changing priority is a two-character edit. The board draws a 3×3 grid (one row per P, one column per U) because each axis has three levels; forcing that into four cells throws information away. ## Built for AI agents `skill/quadrant/` is an agent skill in the `SKILL.md` shape used by Claude Agent Skills, pi, Cursor and friends. Drop it into your agent's skills directory and it knows: - which file a sentence belongs to ("note this" → inbox, "this week" → active, "someday" → someday, "started watching X" → watch) - how to write without damaging the file (append only, edit one line, per-file newline style, compute the ID) - how to run the board and how to do a weekly review A conversation looks like this: > **You:** note that I want to try a two-week review cycle > **Agent:** wrote to `tasks/0-inbox.md`: `- Try a two-week review cycle` > **You:** turn the API error codes into a table before Friday, it matters > **Agent:** wrote to `tasks/1-active/work/demo-project.md`: > `- [ ] T-261021-18 Turn the API error codes into a table #P2 #U1 #work DDL:2026-10-23` > **You:** done with that one > **Agent:** `- [x] ... DONE:2026-10-23` (two spots changed) Install for pi: ```bash cp -r skill/quadrant ~/.pi/agent/skills/ ``` For Claude Code or any other client that supports skills, copy `skill/quadrant/` into its skills directory. Clients without skills support can still use `SKILL.md` as a rules file. ## Board features - **3×3 grid**: one row per P, one column per U; empty cells stay visible - **Search**: title / detail lines / tags / project / directory / ID, case-insensitive, synonym-aware - **Filters**: independent P and U axes, due window, status, directory cascade, tags - **Editing**: click a task for a right-hand drawer (title / P / U / status / DDL / tags) — the layout never shifts - **Write-back**: ticking stamps `DONE:`, plus create, delete and drag, all editing markdown directly - **Focus**: tag tasks `#TopN` and they sort themselves "overdue → today → P1U1 → …" - **Watch**: shows and books in their own tab, no quadrants - **Someday**: cards with a summary, full text on click, draggable in four directions

Drag order is **never written into markdown**: the board keeps one global order in `app/.order.json`, and the secondary panels keep per-panel lists in `app/.lists.json`. Both are derived state — delete them and the default order returns. ## The lineage (what this borrows, honestly) This is not a new idea so much as a careful recombination of well-known ones: - **Importance × urgency** comes from the **Eisenhower Matrix** — attributed to Dwight D. Eisenhower's "what is important is seldom urgent" remark, and popularised for ordinary people by **Stephen R. Covey** in *The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People* (1989). Quadrant nudges it from 2×2 to **3×3**, because a two-level axis forces you to lie about "medium". - **The capture inbox, the "someday/maybe" list and the weekly review** are the three habits that make **David Allen's _Getting Things Done_** (2001) work. This system takes exactly those three and drops the rest. - **One line per task, greppable, plain text** follows the **todo.txt** convention (Gina Trapani, 2007) and the wider local-first / plain-text movement around **Obsidian** — files over databases, `git` over sync services. - **Agent-native packaging** follows **Anthropic's Agent Skills** (`SKILL.md`): the operating manual ships next to the data, so any agent can pick it up. - The first draft of the markdown contract was written with **Doubao** (ByteDance's assistant) in October 2026, then reshaped over two weeks of daily use: the 3×3 grid, the three tracks, the global total order and the "touch one line" write-back rules all came from things that broke in practice. If you are here from the productivity side: the interesting part is not the grid, it is that **the file is the API**. ## Code layout ``` app/ FastAPI backend + React frontend (no third-party UI or drag library) parser.py read-only: scan, parse, filter, group, Focus ordering writer.py write-back: touch one line, re-parse and verify, restore on mismatch order.py board order: one global total order, stored in .order.json lists.py panel order: per-scope lists in .lists.json synonyms.py synonym table shared by search, tag filters and Focus web/ React 19 + TS + Vite (already built into dist/) skill/quadrant/ agent skill: SKILL.md + references (grammar, layout, recipes, panel, review) templates/tasks/ the data-directory template copied by init_tasks.py scripts/ init_tasks.py, screenshot.mjs ``` ## Tests ```bash cd app && uv run python run_tests.py # 100+ assertions, all in temp directories ``` ## Design trade-offs (on purpose) - **Order is not in markdown**: writing it there means reordering files on every drag, huge diffs, and a fight between "human edits the md" and "the board drags". - **Grouping ≠ filtering**: due buckets are mutually exclusive; the `due=week` filter is a rolling seven days including today. - **The date in the ID is the creation date**: no collisions across years and no "what number am I on" bookkeeping. - **No cloud sync**: the data is your files, sync them with git / Syncthing / iCloud. ## Roadmap - [ ] Edit detail lines in the drawer - [ ] Savable multi-filter views - [ ] Indexing / caching beyond a few thousand tasks - [ ] (done in this release) fully English UI and docs ## License MIT
